chapters.title: Chapter 2662 Extractors
paragraphs: "Go ahead. Absorb the energy in this Unknown Ore and Unknown Crystal."
Yuan accepted them and held one in each hand before absorbing their Eternal Essence.
"Done."
A moment later, he handed them back to the individual in white.
"That fast?!"
They didn't dare to believe it, but after examining the Unknown Ore and Unknown Crystal, they had no choice but to believe it.
"I don't get it. If you absorbed so much Limitless, why hasn't your cultivation shown any results?" one of them questioned out loud.
Yuan shrugged and said, "I don't know. As a matter of fact, I didn't even realize my physique had this power until you dragged me here."
"What now, Senior Zhang?" asked another individual in white.
"We will need some time to decide what to do with this information," said Senior Zhang.
"Until then, we'll have to keep you here," she added while looking at Yuan.
Mei Feng then said, "Sorry, but that won't do. He'll be heading to the assembly with the Supreme General in three days."
"You can just find someone else to go."
"That won't be possible, either."
"Why is that?" Senior Zhang asked.
"That isn't something I can disclose to you," Mei Feng replied.
"Even though we have the same Credential Rank?"

"We may have the same Credential Rank, but our clearances are still different. While there is information within this facility that I'm not authorized to access, there is also military-related information that you're not authorized to know, since you're not a soldier."
"Three days, right? He'll remain here until then. I doubt we'll need any longer than that," Senior Zhang said.

"I can accept that, but what is there even to consider? He possesses a never-before-seen physique, and while it's true that he's been turning in defective Unknown Ores and Crystals, he claims he wasn't aware of it. I believe him, too. After all, how could he have possibly known when the Unknown Ores remain completely unchanged in appearance even after their energy has been drained?"
"I'm not going to argue with you here. Three days. You'll have your answer in three days."
As much as Mei Feng wanted to free Yuan, there was truly nothing she could do in this situation.
"Don't worry, I'll be fine," Yuan said.
Mei Feng nodded and left shortly after with Ironwoman.
Meanwhile, Yuan was taken to another room, already furnished like a bedroom.
"You are prohibited from leaving until we say so," Senior Zhang said to him.
After locking Yuan inside the room, Senior Zhang and the others left to discuss the situation.
Inside Mei Feng's office, she and the Ironwoman also had their own discussion.
"What do you think?" Mei Feng asked. "Is Sergeant Yuan telling the truth?"
The Ironwoman closed her eyes to recall everything she'd seen in the Black Zone.
"Hard to say, since we don't know much, if anything, about the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique. However, I do believe he was lying when he said he didn't know until today," Ironwoman said.
"Is that so?"
Despite declaring she believed Yuan, Mei Feng also doubted it.
"It's obvious that he's hiding a lot from us, but who doesn't have secrets? I'm sure he has his reasons," said the Ironwoman. "Most importantly, I don't feel worried even knowing that."
"The biggest question right now is what they—the Extractors—will do about it."

The Extractors were the individuals dressed in white. Although they weren't soldiers, their Credential Ranks were higher than those of most military personnel due to the importance of their work, which involved extracting Limitless from Unknown Ores and Unknown Crystals.

Of course, this wasn't a job that just anyone could apply for. One could become an Extractor only through a personal invitation from the Supreme General, after undergoing a lengthy and rigorous vetting process.
Three days passed in the blink of an eye.
"Damn it... I thought this would be a simple decision..." Senior Zhang sighed as she sank back into her chair, looking defeated after they failed to reach a decision on how to deal with Yuan.
"Quite frankly, I think this is beyond us. Let's just speak with the Supreme General and have him decide," one of the Extractors suggested.
"I agree.
"Fine. I'll speak with the Supreme General," Senior Zhang sighed aloud.
Some time later, she called the Supreme General and revealed the entire situation to him.
The Supreme General did not speak for several minutes as he pondered.
Eventually, he responded, "Let him go. I'll deal with him myself."
"Understood."
Senior Zhang did not question the Supreme General's decision and immediately released Yuan.
"Am I free to go?" Yuan asked.
"I guess so," said Senior Zhang, not revealing everything.
Yuan had expected them to at least warn him against touching any more Unknown Ores or Unknown Crystals, but to his surprise, they said nothing and simply let him leave without another word.
After leaving, Yuan went straight to Mei Feng, who was just as surprised by the outcome as he was.
"What? They simply let you leave without saying anything? There's no way they'd let this matter go so easily. Something is definitely going on, so don't let your guard down," she warned.
"What now?" Yuan asked a moment later.

"Until we have a clearer understanding of the situation, all you can do is carry on as usual. In any case, your escort mission has already been approved, so you'll be accompanying the Supreme General to the assembly."
"Alright."
"Also, I shouldn't have to say this, but refrain from touching any more Unknown Ores and Unknown Crystals from now on," Mei Feng added.
"Of course." Yuan calmly nodded.

Even without Mei Feng's warning, he had already decided to stop absorbing their energy—or at the very least, stop turning in the ones he had drained. After all, he could obtain far more Eternal Essence by defeating Void Specters in the level 2 Black Zone.
"Head to the Parade Deck within the next hour," Mei Feng said shortly later.
"Alright. See you later."
Yuan bid her farewell and left the office.

chapters.title: Chapter 2663 Supreme General
paragraphs: After leaving Mei Feng's office, Yuan immediately made his way to the Parade Deck since he had no need to prepare.
On his way to the Parade Deck, Yuan bumped into a familiar face.
"Did you just meet with my mother?" Mei Xiaoyun asked after noticing the direction he was coming from.
"Yes, she sent me on a new mission."
"A mission directly from a General, huh? It must be fairly important."
"Well, I will be escorting the Supreme General."
"The Supreme General?!" Mei Xiaoyun's eyes widened with surprise after hearing this.
"I hear that despite being the highest-ranking in the military, he's rarely seen," she said a moment later.
"Do you want to see him? He'll be at the Parade Deck in an hour."
Mei Xiaoyun pondered for a moment before nodding her head, as she was too curious about the Supreme General to pass such an opportunity.
Thus, the two of them made their way to the Parade Deck together.
As they walked, Mei Xiaoyun asked, "Any progress with the squad? Or am I still the only member?"
"Uh... I haven't really had the time to recruit anyone, but I will definitely prioritize it once I return from this mission," said Yuan.
"Is that so? Quite frankly, it's better to take things slow since it's more important to find people that we can trust."
"Don't worry, I don't intend on inviting just anyone to the squad."
"Good to know."
Eventually, they arrived at the Parade Deck—or at least, they were about to enter the area when they encountered a line of soldiers blocking the path.
"The Parade Deck is closed today," one of the soldiers informed them.
"I'm Sergeant Yuan, and I am supposed to show up at the Parade Deck for a mission."
"Please give me a moment to verify."
The soldier retrieved a list of names, and after he verified Yuan's name was on it, he nodded and said, "You may enter."
He then turned to look at Mei Xiaoyun, seemingly waiting for her to identify herself.
"I'm not on the mission," she admitted.
"Then you won't be able to enter."
Mei Xiaoyun calmly nodded.
"Looks like I'll have to wait for another chance to see the Supreme General," she turned to Yuan and said.
"Sorry."
"It's fine. Whatever you're doing, stay safe."
"I will."
Yuan continued making his way to the Parade Deck while Mei Xiaoyun turned around and walked in the opposite direction.
A few minutes later, Yuan arrived at the Parade Deck.
The Parade Deck was usually crowded with soldiers who'd go there to socialize or train, but today, it was basically completely empty.
"I was beginning to worry that you might not be able to participate in the mission," said the Ironwoman when she noticed him.
"So, what happened? Are you good?" she then asked.
Yuan shook his head and explained, "I don't know. They allowed me to go without saying anything. General Mei said it's too suspicious and that they might be up to something."
"That definitely does sound suspicious," she muttered.
While Ironwoman fell silent in thought, Yuan shifted his attention to the other two individuals standing not far away on the Parade Deck.
He recognized one of them as the Colonel who had lasted the third longest during the drill.
The other, however, he didn't recognize in the slightest, and he was a Major just like the Ironwoman.
"Who are they?" Yuan asked.
"Colonel Gu and Major Gu."
"...Are you serious?" Yuan looked at her with a dumbfounded face.
"Yes, I am serious."
Yuan shook his head and sighed, "Just how big is their family?"
"Big enough to have at least one 'Gu' in every single rank," she said.
"Honestly, I'm impressed.
Suddenly, the two of them began walking in Yuan's direction.
"Are you sure you're in the right place, Sergeant Yuan?" Major Gu asked once they stopped a few meters away.
Before Yuan could respond, Colonel Gu spoke, "I heard you got arrested recently. By the Extractors, no less."
"Indeed, I was arrested. But as you can see, I am free, so it was just a misunderstanding."
"That's not what I heard," remarked Colonel Gu.
"Oh? Then what did you hear?"
"Don't worry about it," Colonel Gu said, his lips curling into a cold grin.
Yuan and Colonel Gu silently stared at each other, neither willing to look away as the atmosphere between them gradually grew cold and heavy.
"You..." Colonel Gu opened his mouth to speak, but stopped when several powerful presences suddenly appeared on the Parade Deck.

Yuan and the others immediately turned toward the source and saw a group of seven soldiers, six in black outfits that looked more like armor than suits, their faces completely concealed behind full helmets.

As for the seven individual, he was a healthy-looking old man with long white hair and a neatly trimmed beard. Unlike the others, he wore a white outfit that was adorned with medals and three distinct crimson stars.
"We greet the Supreme General."
The Ironwoman and the two from the Gu Family saluted.
When Yuan saw this, he quickly followed and saluted him.
"At ease," said the Supreme General.
"It's been a while, Ironwoman. How's General Mei doing these days?" he said a moment later.
"The same as usual," she calmly replied.

"That's good to hear. I've been wanting to visit her, but my schedule was too full, and just as I was about to go on a break, I had this assembly shoved down my throat. I really cannot wait until my retirement," he sighed aloud.
The Supreme General glanced at Colonel Gu and Major Gu, but his gaze lingered on them for barely half a second before shifting to Yuan, not even bothering to acknowledge their presence.

"Sergeant Yuan... I've heard quite a lot about you. Despite being a relatively new soldier, your achievements have been nothing short of astonishing. In fact, some of your achievements are so unbelievable that even now, I find them difficult to believe."
The Supreme General openly praised Yuan, which irritated Colonel Gu and Major Gu even more than being ignored.

chapters.title: Chapter 2664 Supreme General(2)
paragraphs: "Anyway, although I would like to talk more, we need to set out for the assembly immediately, as we're already running behind schedule. We'll talk more during the journey," said the Supreme General before he turned to look at one of his soldiers and gave a silent nod.
The next moment, the soldier retrieved a palm-sized object and tossed it into the air.
Just as it reached the peak of its ascent, the object rapidly expanded, transforming into a full-sized ship roughly as large as two buses placed side by side.
The ship also did not descend and remained in the air, hovering in place.
'A flying treasure, huh?' Yuan thought to himself.
This was his first time seeing one in this world, not including the flying hoverboards he'd seen before, since they were essentially flying swords in his eyes.
Without a word, the Supreme General and the others jumped aboard the flying treasure.
"You don't look surprised at all, as if you'd seen it before," the Ironwoman remarked as she gazed at his face.
Flying treasures were exceedingly rare in this world and couldn't be purchased with money, as they were considered property of the city itself.
Naturally, this meant that the flying treasure before them didn't belong to the Supreme General personally; he had merely been granted permission to use it for the mission.
"Perhaps I have," Yuan responded with a smile before jumping onto it.

Once everyone was aboard the flying treasure, the controller activated it. However, instead of flying forward like an ordinary vessel, it tore open the void and entered directly into it, traveling through the void itself.
Yet, the flying treasure remained within the void for only a few seconds before returning to the surface. By the time it emerged, they were already several hundred miles beyond the city walls.
Yuan initially assumed the flying treasure needed some time to recover before it could enter the void again. However, it continued flying normally afterward without doing so.
"Is this flying treasure incapable of traveling through the void continuously? It would make traveling much faster if it could," he asked Ironwoman.
"Do you have any idea how much energy that consumes? We only use that function when entering or leaving the city, or in a life-or-death situation," Ironwoman replied.
"That sounds... a little strange. Why can't it just fly in and out of the city normally?"

"Because this flying treasure has built-in functions that block all forms of surveillance. Unfortunately, those same functions also interfere with nearby signals, so flying it through the city normally would cause too much disruption. Also, it doesn't use much energy to leave the city. Using it to travel to the assembly is an entirely different story."
Yuan looked around and then said, "Are we not worried about the Void Hunter? We have eleven people here, so there's a chance for it to appear."

"Another special feature of this flying treasure is that it completely conceals our presence, so as far as the outside world is concerned, we essentially don't exist. In other words, the Void Hunter won't appear," she quickly explained.
"And how certain are you that it actually works that way, rather than simply having been lucky so far?"
The Ironwoman fell silent, as she was unable to answer his question with certainty.

"Don't worry. The Void Hunter won't appear. We've conducted extensive research on this, including tests with over a hundred people aboard for months at a time. If we combined the duration of every test we've conducted, it would amount to decades," the Supreme General suddenly said.
Yuan turned his head to see the Supreme General approaching them.
"Let's continue our conversation, shall we?" he added.
"I wouldn't consider that a conversation," Yuan remarked with a smile.
"Well, you're not wrong. In any case, follow me. I have a few questions for you."
Without waiting for a response, the Supreme General turned around and walked toward the rear of the ship, where a single private room was located.
Yuan quietly followed him into the room.
Once inside, the Supreme General sat behind a small desk and gestured toward the seat across from him, where Yuan sat down.
However, even after several moments had passed, the Supreme General remained silent, merely staring at Yuan with an intense, unreadable gaze.
"So, what did you want to talk to me about?" Yuan asked, breaking the silence.
"I'll get straight to the point...
The Supreme General spoke in a cold, serious tone, his demeanor so different from before that he seemed like an entirely different person.
"Who are you? Where did you come from? And why are you in our city?"
Despite the sudden and drastic shift in the Supreme General, Yuan remained calm as he responded, "I don't understand."

"Did you really think I wouldn't look into your profile? Not only is your history completely blank until just a few months before you joined the military, but you even possess the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique—something General Mei deliberately concealed from the military!"
The Supreme General continued, "I am also aware of your recent arrest and the reason behind it."
"Is it a crime to possess the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique?" Yuan asked.
"No, but your existence is far too suspicious not to raise any alarms. I've lived for many, many years and seen countless things, yet none of them compare to the anomaly that is you."
Yuan fell silent as he contemplated how he should respond to the Supreme General.
The Supreme General realized this and did not rush him to answer.
After some consideration, Yuan responded, "To answer your questions... I am Yuan, and I am from another world. As for my purpose in this city... I wish to meet Gaia."
The Supreme General's eyes widened, looking dazed by his response.
"You are from another world? Are you admitting to being a Celestial Being?" he then asked.
Yuan chuckled, "Me? A Celestial Being? Of course not. I am human."

If we combined the duration of every test we've conducted, it would amount to decades," the Supreme General suddenly said.
Yuan turned his head to see the Supreme General approaching them.
"Let's continue our conversation, shall we?" he added.
"I wouldn't consider that a conversation," Yuan remarked with a smile.
"Well, you're not wrong.
In any case, follow me.
I have a few questions for you."
Without waiting for a response, the Supreme General turned around and walked toward the rear of the ship, where a single private room was located.
Yuan quietly followed him into the room.
Once inside, the Supreme General sat behind a small desk and gestured toward the seat across from him, where Yuan sat down.
However, even after several moments had passed, the Supreme General remained silent, merely staring at Yuan with an intense, unreadable gaze.
"So, what did you want to talk to me about?" Yuan asked, breaking the silence.
"I'll get straight to the point...
The Supreme General spoke in a cold, serious tone, his demeanor so different from before that he seemed like an entirely different person.
"Who are you?
Where did you come from?
And why are you in our city?"
Despite the sudden and drastic shift in the Supreme General, Yuan remained calm as he responded, "I don't understand."
"Did you really think I wouldn't look into your profile?

Not only is your history completely blank until just a few months before you joined the military, but you even possess the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique—something General Mei deliberately concealed from the military!"
The Supreme General continued, "I am also aware of your recent arrest and the reason behind it."
"Is it a crime to possess the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique?" Yuan asked.
"No, but your existence is far too suspicious not to raise any alarms.
I've lived for many, many years and seen countless things, yet none of them compare to the anomaly that is you."
Yuan fell silent as he contemplated how he should respond to the Supreme General.
The Supreme General realized this and did not rush him to answer.
After some consideration, Yuan responded, "To answer your questions...
I am Yuan, and I am from another world.
As for my purpose in this city...
I wish to meet Gaia."
The Supreme General's eyes widened, looking dazed by his response.
"You are from another world?
Are you admitting to being a Celestial Being?" he then asked.
Yuan chuckled, "Me?
A Celestial Being?
Of course not.
I am human."

chapters.title: Chapter 2665 The Union
paragraphs: "Can you prove that you're human?"
The Supreme General narrowed his eyes at Yuan.
"That's an unfair question," Yuan replied calmly. "If I asked you the same thing, how would you prove it?"
After a moment of silence, the Supreme General nodded. "Fair enough."
Indeed, even he wouldn't be able to provide such evidence immediately, as the question itself was inherently difficult to prove.
"Then let's move on to the next question. Why do you want to meet Gaia?"
Yuan shrugged.
"Believe it or not, I'm still trying to figure that out myself. All I know is that I need to meet them."
"If you want to meet Gaia, you'll first have to prove to us that you can be trusted—and that you're not a threat."
"And how am I supposed to do that when you're already suspicious of my very existence?"
"Can you blame us?" the Supreme General sneered. "You appeared out of nowhere with no history whatsoever. Your combat experience and achievements far exceed what should logically be possible."
It was Yuan's turn to fall silent.
Considering the subject of the upcoming assembly and his involvement in it, earning the Supreme General's trust would undoubtedly become even more difficult—if not outright impossible.
"I understand. I'll do my best to earn your trust," Yuan said a moment later.

"I'll be keeping a close eye on you, Sergeant Yuan. If you do anything suspicious, or if I determine that you pose a threat to our city or Gaia, I'll personally put you down," the Supreme General said solemnly.
Yuan left the room shortly after, returning to the Ironwoman's side.
"What did you talk about?" she inquired.
"The Supreme General doesn't trust me," he admitted.
"I'm not surprised."
"Really?" Yuan was slight surprised by her response.

"If it weren't for General Mei, I also would have a hard time trusting you," she admitted. "Whether it's your background or actions, your entire existence is shrouded in mysteries and secrets. If you want to earn the Supreme General's trust, you'll have to stop being so secretive."
Yuan raised an eyebrow and asked, "What about you? Does the Supreme General trust you?"
"Of course. The public may not know my identity, but the Supreme General is fully aware of my background. It's impossible to completely hide your identity in the military, after all."
"I see..."
After a brief pause, the Ironwoman continued, "While we're on the subject, I watched a replay of our drill."
"And?"
"I saw your performance. You were holding back, weren't you?"
"What if I was?"
"Things like that make people wonder, which breeds doubt and suspicion. I'm not saying that's how I feel, but it's a common reaction.
Yuan let out a deep sigh before speaking.

"What do you want me to do, really? On one hand, you're telling me not to reveal certain things because they could cause trouble, and on the other, you're saying I'm making myself look suspicious by doing exactly that."
"Sorry, but I don't know how to answer that. I guess it's about finding a balance, so you appear trustworthy without revealing everything."
"I'll keep that in mind."
Meanwhile, inside his office, the Supreme General sat back in his seat with a pondering expression.
"He wants to meet Gaia, huh? What a coincidence," he mumbled.
'But I wasn't expecting him to reveal that he's from another world...' he thought.
"General Mei... what sort of entity did you bring into the military?" he sighed aloud.
Time passed swiftly, and two weeks had gone by since they began their journey.
"Just where does this assembly take place, anyway?" Yuan suddenly asked.
"At the center of this world, the Union."
"The Union? Is it merely a place built for the assembly, or is there more to it?"
"It's a city."
"Huh? I thought the assembly didn't take place in any of the nine cities—at least, that's what General Mei told me." Yuan raised his eyebrows, looking puzzled.
"It doesn't. The Union is a city, but it's a neutral territory and isn't counted among the nine cities. It's also the smallest city in existence."
"Neutral?"

"It means the Union doesn't swear allegiance to any of the nine cities and acts solely in its own interests. If any one of the nine cities attempts to influence or control it, the other eight are permitted to unite against that city," she elaborated.

"Also, once you set foot in the Union, your identity is essentially stripped away, so your background no longer matters. In other words, if you get into a conflict with someone from another city, neither side can use their background to retaliate or seek compensation afterward."
"That's only while you're in the city, right? What if they come after you once you leave the place?"
"That's why most visitors tend to wear masks or disguises when they are in the Union."
"If it's so safe over there, why is there even a need for escorts?" Yuan then asked, wondering about their real purpose.

"Quite frankly, we're not here to protect the Supreme General. I mean, if something happens, we'll obviously ensure his safety, but his squad is already more than capable of doing that. We're mostly here as trophies—a way for our city to show off its best soldiers to the other cities," Ironwoman revealed the true purpose of their presence.

"Quite frankly, we're not here to protect the Supreme General. I mean, if something happens, we'll obviously ensure his safety, but his squad is already more than capable of doing that. We're mostly here as trophies—a way for our city to show off its best soldiers to the other cities," Ironwoman revealed the true purpose of their presence.
"Have you been to an assembly before?" Yuan continued to ask.
"No, this is also my first time going to one."
After another week of traveling, the Supreme General left his office for the first time.
"We'll be arriving at the Union soon. Prepare yourselves."
"Yes, Supreme General!"
A few hours later, the flying treasure began to slow, eventually coming to a complete stop before the towering walls of the Union.
Shortly afterward, a group of individuals dressed in gray and black uniforms approached their flying treasure.
"Welcome to the Union. Please identify yourselves and tell us the reason for visiting," one of them said.
The Supreme General stepped forward and announced, "I am Supreme General Tian Xizhi of Gaia's Heaven, and these are my soldiers. We're here for the assembly."
One of his black-suited soldiers then approached the Union soldier and presented their identification, confirming the group's identity.
After confirming their identity, the Union soldiers saluted them and said, "Thank you for your cooperation, Supreme General Tian. Please follow us."
The flying treasure began moving again, slowly following the group of soldiers.
Meanwhile, Yuan turned to look at the Supreme General and asked, "Your surname is Tian? Are you related to Tian Yuchen?"
"Tian Yuchen is my grandfather. Why are you asking?" The Supreme General revealed.
"I was just curious..." Yuan replied before falling silent.
The Supreme General narrowed his eyes at Yuan but didn't speak further.
Once they entered the city, the Union soldiers guided their flying treasure to an empty docking area, where they landed and disembarked.
Then they were brought to a nearby teleporter, where they teleported to another area.

"There are still five days until the assembly. Please stay here until then. We will remind you the day before. Of course, you're free to leave and wander the city as you wish. If you need anything, don't hesitate to let the servants know, and we'll do our best to accommodate you."
The Union soldiers didn't linger and left swiftly, keeping things short and simple.
Once they were alone, the Supreme General pointed to a certain building there and said, "That is mine."
Then he pointed at the largest building next and continued, "My soldiers, the Midnight Squad, will live there. The rest of you can figure out the rest. Any questions?"
Yuan raised his hand and said, "I'd like to explore this place."
"I don't care what you do, as long as you return before the assembly," he said.
"Anything I should keep in mind?" Yuan then asked.
"Use your common sense."
After saying that, the Supreme General turned around and walked into the building he had picked for himself.
The Midnight Squad also retired into their building.
The Gu Family randomly picked one of the available buildings there and entered it shortly after, leaving Yuan and the Ironwoman lingering outside.
"Are you not going to pick a place?" Yuan asked her.
Ironwoman silently stared at Yuan, as if contemplating something.
After a moment of silence, she turned around and began walking away.
"Try not to cause any trouble," she said before swiftly disappearing into one of the unoccupied buildings.
She had considered accompanying Yuan to ensure his safety, but quickly realized there was little reason to worry about someone who had outlasted her during the drill.
Yuan had expected to receive a list of rules to follow while exploring the city, but when none came, he simply shrugged and approached one of the many maids stationed around the buildings.
"Can you give me a brief explanation of the city and how I can get out of here? I'd like to look around."

chapters.title: Chapter 2666 The Union(2)
paragraphs: "Most certainly, esteemed guest."

The maid gave a courteous bow before explaining, "The Union is split into five districts. The Southern District, Northern District, Western District, Eastern District, and the Central District, and we're currently in the Central District."

"Since our city is quite small, we only have two teleportation devices, both of which you've already used, so you'll have to travel on foot if you wish to explore the city. This area is only accessible through the teleport device, so you'll have to use it to enter and leave this place."
"I see. Thanks for the information," Yuan said.
Just as he turned around and began walking away, the maid spoke again, "Excuse me, but are you going to leave without a disguise?"
Yuan halted after hearing such words, and he recalled what the Ironwoman told him before they arrived at the Union.
"I don't have any mask on me," he said.
"We can provide that for you," she said with a smile.
"In that case..." Yuan nodded.
"Please follow me."
Yuan proceeded to follow the maid to another building about ten minutes away.
The interior of this building was just a long hallway with several rooms.
"Just enter any of these rooms and choose whichever disguise you like best," the maid gave a quick explanation.
"Alright."
Yuan walked into the room closest to the exit and was surprised to find it was essentially a massive walk-in closet, filled with thousands of masks and outfits ready for him.
Since he wasn't picky about his appearance, he swiftly picked an ordinary black mask and a black outfit that fit perfectly to match it.
After spending not even five minutes inside, Yuan left the room and returned to the maid.
"I'm done."
"Then I will take you to the teleporter now," she said.
Shortly later, they arrived at the teleport device.
"You can step on the teleport device whenever you are ready," she said.
Yuan stepped onto the device the next moment and said, "Thanks for the help."
"I don't deserve it, as I am only doing my job," she replied with a calm smile.
The next moment, Yuan vanished from the teleport device and returned to the docking area.
Then, he randomly picked one direction and walked in it.

As he walked through the streets, Yuan noticed that while there were many people wearing masks like him, there weren't nearly as many as he had expected. In fact, roughly ninety percent of the people walked around openly with their faces uncovered.
Of course, he knew these people were likely locals, since only those from another city had any reason to keep their identity hidden.
The buildings in the city weren't particularly impressive, either. Compared to Gaia's Heaven, where skyscrapers were a common sight, most of the buildings here were no more than four stories tall.
After walking for some time and passing by many shops, Yuan stopped before a restaurant and stared at it in silence, thinking to himself that he hadn't really eaten anything in a long time.
'I have some money from handing in Unknown Ores and Crystals... but how do I use it?'
Since he never had the opportunity to spend money, he never learned how to pay using the system.
After pondering for a bit, Yuan decided to enter the restaurant.
"Hello. Will you be dining alone?"
"Yes."
"Do you mind sharing a table with another customer? We're a bit full right now. Otherwise, you'll have to wait."
"I don't mind."
"Great. Please follow me."
Yuan followed the waiter to his table, where another masked customer was already seated across from him, her attention focused entirely on the menu in her hands.
Yuan gave the individual a quick glance as he sat down, but swiftly turned his attention to the menu.
After looking through the menu to ensure he had enough money to pay for it, he gestured toward a waiter.
"Hello, are you ready to order?"
Yuan nodded and said, "I want one of everything on the menu. You can send them out one at a time since there is limited space."
"E-Everything on the menu?"
Not just the waiter; even the one seated in front of Yuan looked surprised.
"Yes."
After a moment of silence, the waiter snapped out of his daze and said, "My apologies, but for an order this large, we'll require payment upfront..."
Yuan nodded. "Sure."
"Please give me a moment."
The waiter left, then returned a few moments later with a palm-sized device with a crystal orb embedded in it.
Yuan didn't ask any questions and placed his palm onto the crystal orb.
<Maple's Dining has requested a payment of 7,122 Gaia Credits>
'Looks like Gaia Credits are universal...' Yuan thought to himself as he confirmed the payment.
Once the waiter confirmed the payment, he bowed to Yuan and said, "Thank you for the payment. Your food will be out as soon as possible."
"I am also ready to order."
The individual sitting across from Yuan suddenly said.
Yuan raised an eyebrow after hearing her voice, as it sounded quite familiar.
"Of course. What would you like?"
"I'll have the A-4, C-6, and a C-7."
While the woman placed her order, Yuan quietly examined her.
She had light brown hair tied into a bun at the back of her head and hazel-colored eyes.
Once the waiter walked away, the woman removed her white mask and placed it on her lap.
Yuan's eyes widened slightly upon seeing her face.
"Lulu..." Yuan muttered, as the woman before her looked exactly like Chu Liuxiang.
"Excuse me?" The woman looked at him with raised eyebrows.
"Hm? Oh, I was just talking to myself," he quickly said.
"Is that so?"
The woman didn't say anything else and quietly waited for her food.
A few minutes later, Yuan's food arrived first.
"Thanks."
Yuan removed his mask before eating.
The woman, who had been minding her own business, suddenly started staring at Yuan while he ate.
Yuan noticed that he was being watched, but he paid it no mind and continued eating in silence.
By the time he finished his first dish, the second had already arrived, followed shortly by the third.
When Yuan's seventh dish was brought to the table, the woman finally received her first.
Time passed swiftly, and before he realized it, Yuan had finished every single dish on the menu. Meanwhile, the woman across from him was just starting her final dish.
"I have never seen anyone eat even half as much as you just did," the woman suddenly remarked.
"It's a hobby," Yuan replied with a smile.
"Is that so?"
Yuan then asked, "Which city are you from?"
"Spirit City. What about you?"
"Gaia's Heaven."
"Did you come here just to eat?" she then asked.
"Maybe. Why are you here?"
"Sorry, but I can't tell you."
"Is that so?"
Yuan didn't question her any further, and a moment later, he stood up.
"See you later."
"You make it sound as though we're guaranteed to meet again," she remarked.
"I have a feeling we will."
The woman raised an eyebrow but didn't respond.
Yuan left shortly afterward and continued wandering through the city, stopping by several other restaurants along the way.
Eventually, he arrived before a ten-story building, one of the tallest structures he had seen in the city thus far.
"Union's Treasury."
After reading the sign above the large entrance, Yuan entered the building.
The building was basically a shopping mall, with the first floor selling all sorts of weapons.
Yuan approached one of the stores and peeked at the prices.
"Two hundred million credits?" His eyes widened slightly at the staggering price.

After turning in ten thousand Unknown Ores, Yuan had received ten million credits, which he initially thought was a fortune, especially considering the cost of his meals. However, after seeing the price of the weapon, he quickly realized that wasn't the case.
'I think I am beginning to understand why the military doesn't provide a weapon to every soldier...' Yuan thought to himself.

He visited several other stores to compare prices and was surprised to discover that the first store had actually been one of the cheaper ones, with some weapons elsewhere costing over a billion credits.
"Why do the prices vary so drastically? They all look the same to me," Yuan asked one of the sellers.

"They may look identical on the outside, but their functions differ greatly. Some have a higher capacity, allowing the user to channel more Limitless through them, while others are designed for greater efficiency."
"How do they compare to military weapons?" Yuan asked curiously.

"That's difficult to say, since every military uses its own specialized weapons. Generally speaking, military weapons are superior at the higher end. However, when it comes to standard equipment, publicly available weapons are usually better."
"How can you tell whether a weapon is high-end?"
"All high-end weapons can draw upon external sources, such as Unknown Ores, to increase their power, while standard weapons rely solely on the wielder's Limitless."
"I see..."
Yuan thanked the seller for the information before heading to the second floor, where the stores shifted from selling weapons to techniques.
And moments after he entered the second floor, he noticed a certain individual standing outside one of the stores.
Yuan approached this individual with a smile behind his mask.
"I guess my feeling was right," he said, prompting the individual to turn to look at him with her hazel-colored eyes.
"Did you follow me?" she asked.
"Are you calling me a stalker? That's rude." Yuan shook his head. "It's a coincidence."

Will you be dining alone?"
"Yes."
"Do you mind sharing a table with another customer?
We're a bit full right now.
Otherwise, you'll have to wait."
"I don't mind."
"Great.
Please follow me."
Yuan followed the waiter to his table, where another masked customer was already seated across from him, her attention focused entirely on the menu in her hands.
Yuan gave the individual a quick glance as he sat down, but swiftly turned his attention to the menu.
After looking through the menu to ensure he had enough money to pay for it, he gestured toward a waiter.
"Hello, are you ready to order?"
Yuan nodded and said, "I want one of everything on the menu.
You can send them out one at a time since there is limited space."
"E-Everything on the menu?"
Not just the waiter; even the one seated in front of Yuan looked surprised.
"Yes."
After a moment of silence, the waiter snapped out of his daze and said, "My apologies, but for an order this large, we'll require payment upfront..."
Yuan nodded.
"Sure."
"Please give me a moment."
The waiter left, then returned a few moments later with a palm-sized device with a crystal orb embedded in it.
Yuan didn't ask any questions and placed his palm onto the crystal orb.
<Maple's Dining has requested a payment of 7,122 Gaia Credits>
'Looks like Gaia Credits are universal...' Yuan thought to himself as he confirmed the payment.
Once the waiter confirmed the payment, he bowed to Yuan and said, "Thank you for the payment.
Your food will be out as soon as possible."
"I am also ready to order."
The individual sitting across from Yuan suddenly said.
Yuan raised an eyebrow after hearing her voice, as it sounded quite familiar.
"Of course.
What would you like?"
"I'll have the A-4, C-6, and a C-7."
While the woman placed her order, Yuan quietly examined her.
She had light brown hair tied into a bun at the back of her head and hazel-colored eyes.
Once the waiter walked away, the woman removed her white mask and placed it on her lap.
Yuan's eyes widened slightly upon seeing her face.
"Lulu..." Yuan muttered, as the woman before her looked exactly like Chu Liuxiang.
"Excuse me?" The woman looked at him with raised eyebrows.
"Hm?
Oh, I was just talking to myself," he quickly said.
"Is that so?"
The woman didn't say anything else and quietly waited for her food.
A few minutes later, Yuan's food arrived first.
"Thanks."
Yuan removed his mask before eating.
The woman, who had been minding her own business, suddenly started staring at Yuan while he ate.
Yuan noticed that he was being watched, but he paid it no mind and continued eating in silence.
By the time he finished his first dish, the second had already arrived, followed shortly by the third.
When Yuan's seventh dish was brought to the table, the woman finally received her first.
Time passed swiftly, and before he realized it, Yuan had finished every single dish on the menu.
Meanwhile, the woman across from him was just starting her final dish.
"I have never seen anyone eat even half as much as you just did," the woman suddenly remarked.
"It's a hobby," Yuan replied with a smile.
"Is that so?"
Yuan then asked, "Which city are you from?"
"Spirit City.
What about you?"
"Gaia's Heaven."
"Did you come here just to eat?" she then asked.
"Maybe.
Why are you here?"
"Sorry, but I can't tell you."
"Is that so?"
Yuan didn't question her any further, and a moment later, he stood up.
"See you later."
"You make it sound as though we're guaranteed to meet again," she remarked.
"I have a feeling we will."
The woman raised an eyebrow but didn't respond.
Yuan left shortly afterward and continued wandering through the city, stopping by several other restaurants along the way.
Eventually, he arrived before a ten-story building, one of the tallest structures he had seen in the city thus far.
"Union's Treasury."
After reading the sign above the large entrance, Yuan entered the building.
The building was basically a shopping mall, with the first floor selling all sorts of weapons.
Yuan approached one of the stores and peeked at the prices.
"Two hundred million credits?" His eyes widened slightly at the staggering price.
After turning in ten thousand Unknown Ores, Yuan had received ten million credits, which he initially thought was a fortune, especially considering the cost of his meals.
However, after seeing the price of the weapon, he quickly realized that wasn't the case.
'I think I am beginning to understand why the military doesn't provide a weapon to every soldier...' Yuan thought to himself.

He visited several other stores to compare prices and was surprised to discover that the first store had actually been one of the cheaper ones, with some weapons elsewhere costing over a billion credits.
"Why do the prices vary so drastically?
They all look the same to me," Yuan asked one of the sellers.
"They may look identical on the outside, but their functions differ greatly.
Some have a higher capacity, allowing the user to channel more Limitless through them, while others are designed for greater efficiency."
"How do they compare to military weapons?" Yuan asked curiously.
"That's difficult to say, since every military uses its own specialized weapons.
Generally speaking, military weapons are superior at the higher end.
However, when it comes to standard equipment, publicly available weapons are usually better."
"How can you tell whether a weapon is high-end?"
"All high-end weapons can draw upon external sources, such as Unknown Ores, to increase their power, while standard weapons rely solely on the wielder's Limitless."
"I see..."
Yuan thanked the seller for the information before heading to the second floor, where the stores shifted from selling weapons to techniques.
And moments after he entered the second floor, he noticed a certain individual standing outside one of the stores.
Yuan approached this individual with a smile behind his mask.
"I guess my feeling was right," he said, prompting the individual to turn to look at him with her hazel-colored eyes.
"Did you follow me?" she asked.
"Are you calling me a stalker?
That's rude." Yuan shook his head.
"It's a coincidence."

What do you plan on doing with so many Refined Crystals?" Yuan asked in a wary tone, as there were now several billion years' worth of Eternal Essence in her possession."I'm not going to use them all for myself," she explained. "Since Refined Crystals are relatively cheap here compared to my city, my family asked me to purchase some while I'm here."I cannot even begin to fathom why your family needs so much energy..."My family owns a business in another city, and it's operate costs are... not cheap."I see..."Anyways, let's continue. Yuan remarked when he noticed that people were beginning to stare at them."Don't worry, I can protect myself," she said.They proceeded to the fifth floor, repeating the same thing, but the woman spent twice as much as she did on the previous floor.Yuan had become numb to her crazy spending and quietly followed.Suddenly, shortly after they arrived on the sixth floor, Yuan sensed killing intent somewhere on the floor."Be careful. I think you're being targeted," Yuan warned her."Is that so?" The woman replied in a nonchalant manner, as if she wasn't bothered by it in the slightest.The killing intent became clearer and more obvious as time passed.'Four people, huh? They must be working together...' Yuan thought to himself.Although he could sense their killing intent, Yuan couldn't accurately pinpoint their location or the individuals themselves since his cultivation and divine sense were suppressed by the formation in the city, not to mention there were thousands of people wandering the floor.Still, he could estimate the direction of the killing intent and their distance."Hey, there are four people targeting you, and they're closing in," Yuan warned her as the killing intent drew closer to them.The woman didn't respond and quietly nodded her head in acknowledgment.A few moments later, the source of the killing intent was only several meters away, and Yuan sensed it spike sharply—a clear sign that an attack was imminent.Reacting instinctively, Yuan grabbed the woman's hand, preparing to protect her."What are you—"Bang! A loud gunshot rang out before she could finish."Huh?"Just as the woman turned to face Yuan, her eyes widened upon seeing a distinct fist-sized hole in his chest."Hm?"Yuan looked down with a similarly surprised expression. The bullet had struck him directly in the heart.It didn't take long for him to realize that the woman had never been the target, and that he had been the target from the very beginning.Meanwhile, chaos erupted shortly after the gunshot as shouts and screams filled the area. Once people realized what was happening, they began scrambling for the exits."Murder! Someone has been murdered!"The people who saw Yuan's injury shouted as they ran away, not even bothering to confirm whether he was truly dead or not."You..." The woman beside Yuan was too stunned to speak.However, it wasn't the fact that he had been shot that shocked her. What truly surprised her was watching the wound in his chest regenerate before her very eyes."Let's get out of here," Yuan said, leading her out of the building while holding her hand the entire way."How are you still alive?" she asked once they were outside and a safe distance from the building.Yuan glanced down at the hole in his outfit and said, "He missed my heart."The woman stared at the hole again, which was clearly positioned directly over his heart, before looking back at him."That's clearly bullshit. Also, you can let go of me now," she said, her gaze drifting to their hands."Oh, sorry." Yuan apologized as he let go.The woman stared at her hands in a daze. It was the first time anyone had ever held her hand in such a manner, and by a complete stranger, no less.Yet, for some reason, she hadn't disliked it. If anything, she had found the sensation strangely comforting, as though it were completely natural."What's your name?" she then asked."Yuan."I'm Huang Zi Han, and I'm sorry for getting you shot," she suddenly apologized, mistakenly believing that he had been shot while trying to protect her."You don't have to apologize. It wasn't your fault," Yuan said while shaking his head."This city is usually very safe, and I have been here several times without a single incident, so I wasn't worried that anything might happen," Huang Zi Han sighed."Anyway, are you really okay? You don't have to act tough to impress me. If you're worried about the medical bill, I'll pay for it.

chapters.title: Chapter 2668 Wrong Target
paragraphs: "I am really fine. Look. The injury is already gone," Yuan said, proving it by banging on the spot where the bullet had struck with his hands like a gorilla.
"If you say so..." Huang Zi Han muttered.
"Anyway, I should go back now. I don't want to involve you in any more accidents."
"Alright." Yuan nodded.

Normally, he would have offered to accompany her until he was certain she was safe, but there was no need in their current situation. Huang Zi Han wasn't the target, and staying with her would only put her in further danger.
"See you later," he said as she started walking away.
"We'll see about that..." Huang Zi Han replied without looking back.
Once Huang Zi Han disappeared, Yuan continued wandering the city while pondering the situation.
'I can only think of one reason why there's a target on my back...'

The images of Colonel Gu and Major Gu immediately surfaced in his mind. After all, they were the only ones who could have known his identity, since they knew he would be wandering the city and could have easily seen him leave in his new disguise.
Although he had also removed his mask while eating at the restaurants, he couldn't think of any reason why that alone would have made him a target.

While he was the subject of the upcoming assembly, nobody knew he was in the city. And even if someone did, they wouldn't be foolish enough to attack him unprovoked with so many innocent people nearby.
Therefore, Yuan concluded that the Gu Family was most likely responsible for the assassination attempt.
'How bold and reckless of them to attack me here...' he shook his head inwardly.
He was expecting an attack, but he wasn't expecting it to happen on the first day of their arrival.
'They're getting impatient...'

Yuan began pondering how he should deal with the situation. Even if he was convinced that it was the Gu Family who tried to kill him, he had no evidence, and the attackers had vanished after the assassination attempt.
'They probably think I'm already dead and won't make another move until they realize I survived. I should return to the base first and let the Gu Family see that I'm still alive...'
He glanced down at his damaged outfit.
'I need a change of clothes, anyway.'
With that, Yuan made his way back to the Central District.
Back at the base, Yuan approached the same maid who helped him out earlier and said, "Sorry, but can I get a new outfit?"
"Good lord! What happened?! Are you okay?!" The maid gasped in shock when she saw the gaping hole in his outfit.
"Yes, there was an accident, but as you can see, I am fine." Yuan calmly dismissed it.
After snapping out of her daze, the maid nodded and said, "Once you change your outfit, please hand me your old ones."
"Alright."
The maid brought Yuan back to the building with the closet-like rooms.
After changing into a new outfit, Yuan handed his old ones to the maid.
"Thanks."
Instead of returning to wandering the city, Yuan made his way to the building occupied by the Gu Family and knocked on the door.
A few moments later, Major Gu opened the door.
Major Gu's eyes widened in shock, disbelief spreading across his face as though he were staring at a ghost.
"What's wrong? You look like you're seeing a ghost," Yuan remarked, snapping Major Gu out of his daze.
"W-What the hell do you want?" he stuttered.

"I know General Gu doesn't like me, but I just realized we've never even spoken face-to-face. I want you to send him a message for me," Yuan said. "Tell him we can sit down and talk this out like adults, or he can keep playing these games and eventually pay the price.
"You dare to threaten a General?" Major Gu remarked with narrowed eyes.
Yuan shrugged. "I am merely reminding him that there's something called karma. That's all."
After saying such words, Yuan turned around and walked away.
Major Gu stared at Yuan in silence, remaining by the door until he completely vanished.
Then, Major Gu shut the door and called Colonel Gu.
"That bastard is still alive!"
"What?" Colonel Gu raised his eyebrows in puzzlement.
"Sergeant Yuan! That cockroach is still alive!"
"That's impossible! Those guys said that they'd killed him!"
"Either those bastards are lying, or Sergeant Yuan just knocked on the door and had a conversation with me as a corpse—a perfectly healthy-looking corpse!" Major Gu shouted.
"Those bastards! How dare they try to scam us?!"
Colonel Gu immediately picked up his communication device and called a certain number.
"Yes—"
"YOU FUCKERS!" Colonel Gu screamed the moment the call connected.
"W-What?" the person on the other end muttered, sounding dumbfounded.
"Don't you 'what' me, you scamming bastards! Just minutes ago, you called us and claimed that you'd completed the mission and killed the target!"
"But we did kill him! The strike connected, and we all saw a giant hole in his chest where his heart is located!" The man exclaimed.

"Bull-fucking-shit! You're either lying out of your ass, or you killed the wrong guy! Because the target you're supposed to kill just knocked on our door—alive and healthy!" Colonel Gu cursed without reserve.
"What?! That can't be! The target was exactly as you described! He wore..." The man proceeded to describe what Yuan wore perfectly.
"Wait! Sergeant Yuan wasn't wearing those clothes when I spoke with him just now!" Major Gu revealed after hearing it.
"He must have changed his clothes! This explains everything!"

The man then spoke, "In that case, you cannot fault us for killing the wrong target, as we were given false information. If you wish for us to continue this mission, you'll need to pay extra for your mistake and for the inconvenience."
"How much?"
"Three hundred million."
"What?! That's damn near the price of what we already paid!"
"Do you want us to continue the mission or not?"
After a moment of silence, Colonel Gu replied, "We'll send you the payment shortly. Just make sure you actually killed him this time."
"Of course. Our gang has never failed a mission before. Now then... what does he look like now?"
Major Gu swiftly recalled Yuan's new appearance to the assassins.
Meanwhile, Yuan returned to the city and wandered the place as he waited for the assassins to strike again, visiting every restaurant that piqued his interest.
After several hours of eating, Yuan stopped moving when a little boy with teary eyes approached him and said, "Big brother, can you help me?"
"What's up?"
"My mother was taken by some people, and they said if I wanted her back, I needed to tell you to follow me..."
Yuan fell silent.
"Please follow me, big brother. I want my mother back..." the boy spoke again, looking like he was on the verge of bawling his eyes out.
"Alright, take me to them..." Yuan nodded a moment later.
Afterward, Yuan followed the boy for several blocks before they entered a narrow alleyway that ended in a dead end.
"So, where are these strangers and your mother?" Yuan asked without even bothering to look around.
However, the boy didn't respond. Instead, he reached beneath his clothes, pulled out a dagger, and stabbed Yuan in the leg.
However, due to Yuan's physique, the boy lacked the strength to pierce his skin, much less injure him.
The boy's eyes widened in shock, and his body froze as his mind went blank, completely unsure of what to do next.
Yuan calmly turned his head to look at the boy and asked, "What are you doing?"
The boy dropped the knife and began walking back with a fearful expression on his face.
"Hey, where do you—"
Just as Yuan turned to follow him, a silhouette descended from above and landed behind him before thrusting a long blade made of Limitless into his back.
"This weapon has been infused with a poisonous Refined Crystal, so you'll be dead within a minute," the attacker said. "However, if you answer my questions, I'll give you an antidote."
Yuan turned to face him, and the attacker was taken aback by how calm he looked.
"What question?" Yuan inquired.
"Are you Sergeant Yuan?"
"Indeed, I am."
"Thanks. You can die now." The attacker chuckled.
"What about the antidote?"
"Did you really think I'd let you live?"
"No, not really."
The next moment, Yuan collapsed to the ground with a heavy thud.
Shortly afterward, the attacker rolled him onto his back and removed his mask before retrieving a device to take a picture of his face.
"And... sent," the attacker muttered after sending the evidence. "It's been a while since we've had such an easy mission with such a high payout."
"I'd like to hear more about that."
A familiar voice suddenly resounded.
Startled, the attacker dropped the device and turned toward Yuan, who was slowly rising from the ground.
"I-Impossible! How are you still alive?!" he exclaimed.
"Did you really think you could kill me with such weak poison?" Yuan responded with a cold smile.
"Weak?! That wasn't just some ordinary poison! It was one of the strongest poisons in the world!" the attacker revealed.
"If that's the case, then the poisons in this world are quite lacking," Yuan replied calmly. "That said, I'm not surprised. I don't see much need for poison in an environment like this."
"W-Who the hell are you...?"
"Hm? Weren't you paying attention just now? I already told you that I am Sergeant Yuan."

I don't want to involve you in any more accidents."
"Alright." Yuan nodded.
Normally, he would have offered to accompany her until he was certain she was safe, but there was no need in their current situation.
Huang Zi Han wasn't the target, and staying with her would only put her in further danger.
"See you later," he said as she started walking away.
"We'll see about that..." Huang Zi Han replied without looking back.
Once Huang Zi Han disappeared, Yuan continued wandering the city while pondering the situation.
'I can only think of one reason why there's a target on my back...'
The images of Colonel Gu and Major Gu immediately surfaced in his mind.
After all, they were the only ones who could have known his identity, since they knew he would be wandering the city and could have easily seen him leave in his new disguise.
Although he had also removed his mask while eating at the restaurants, he couldn't think of any reason why that alone would have made him a target.
While he was the subject of the upcoming assembly, nobody knew he was in the city.
And even if someone did, they wouldn't be foolish enough to attack him unprovoked with so many innocent people nearby.
Therefore, Yuan concluded that the Gu Family was most likely responsible for the assassination attempt.
'How bold and reckless of them to attack me here...' he shook his head inwardly.
He was expecting an attack, but he wasn't expecting it to happen on the first day of their arrival.
'They're getting impatient...'
Yuan began pondering how he should deal with the situation.
Even if he was convinced that it was the Gu Family who tried to kill him, he had no evidence, and the attackers had vanished after the assassination attempt.
'They probably think I'm already dead and won't make another move until they realize I survived.
I should return to the base first and let the Gu Family see that I'm still alive...'
He glanced down at his damaged outfit.
'I need a change of clothes, anyway.'
With that, Yuan made his way back to the Central District.
Back at the base, Yuan approached the same maid who helped him out earlier and said, "Sorry, but can I get a new outfit?"
"Good lord!
What happened?!
Are you okay?!" The maid gasped in shock when she saw the gaping hole in his outfit.
"Yes, there was an accident, but as you can see, I am fine." Yuan calmly dismissed it.
After snapping out of her daze, the maid nodded and said, "Once you change your outfit, please hand me your old ones."
"Alright."
The maid brought Yuan back to the building with the closet-like rooms.
After changing into a new outfit, Yuan handed his old ones to the maid.
"Thanks."
Instead of returning to wandering the city, Yuan made his way to the building occupied by the Gu Family and knocked on the door.
A few moments later, Major Gu opened the door.
Major Gu's eyes widened in shock, disbelief spreading across his face as though he were staring at a ghost.
"What's wrong?
You look like you're seeing a ghost," Yuan remarked, snapping Major Gu out of his daze.
"W-What the hell do you want?" he stuttered.
"I know General Gu doesn't like me, but I just realized we've never even spoken face-to-face.
I want you to send him a message for me," Yuan said.
"Tell him we can sit down and talk this out like adults, or he can keep playing these games and eventually pay the price.
"You dare to threaten a General?" Major Gu remarked with narrowed eyes.
Yuan shrugged.
"I am merely reminding him that there's something called karma.
That's all."
After saying such words, Yuan turned around and walked away.
Major Gu stared at Yuan in silence, remaining by the door until he completely vanished.
Then, Major Gu shut the door and called Colonel Gu.
"That bastard is still alive!"
"What?" Colonel Gu raised his eyebrows in puzzlement.
"Sergeant Yuan!
That cockroach is still alive!"
"That's impossible!
Those guys said that they'd killed him!"
"Either those bastards are lying, or Sergeant Yuan just knocked on the door and had a conversation with me as a corpse—a perfectly healthy-looking corpse!" Major Gu shouted.
"Those bastards!
How dare they try to scam us?!"
Colonel Gu immediately picked up his communication device and called a certain number.
"Yes—"
"YOU FUCKERS!" Colonel Gu screamed the moment the call connected.
"W-What?" the person on the other end muttered, sounding dumbfounded.
"Don't you 'what' me, you scamming bastards!
Just minutes ago, you called us and claimed that you'd completed the mission and killed the target!"
"But we did kill him!
The strike connected, and we all saw a giant hole in his chest where his heart is located!" The man exclaimed.
"Bull-fucking-shit!
You're either lying out of your ass, or you killed the wrong guy!
Because the target you're supposed to kill just knocked on our door—alive and healthy!" Colonel Gu cursed without reserve.
"What?!
That can't be!
The target was exactly as you described!
He wore..." The man proceeded to describe what Yuan wore perfectly.
"Wait!
Sergeant Yuan wasn't wearing those clothes when I spoke with him just now!" Major Gu revealed after hearing it.
"He must have changed his clothes!
This explains everything!"
The man then spoke, "In that case, you cannot fault us for killing the wrong target, as we were given false information.
If you wish for us to continue this mission, you'll need to pay extra for your mistake and for the inconvenience."
"How much?"
"Three hundred million."
"What?!
That's damn near the price of what we already paid!"
"Do you want us to continue the mission or not?"
After a moment of silence, Colonel Gu replied, "We'll send you the payment shortly.
Just make sure you actually killed him this time."
"Of course.
Our gang has never failed a mission before.
Now then... what does he look like now?"
Major Gu swiftly recalled Yuan's new appearance to the assassins.
Meanwhile, Yuan returned to the city and wandered the place as he waited for the assassins to strike again, visiting every restaurant that piqued his interest.
After several hours of eating, Yuan stopped moving when a little boy with teary eyes approached him and said, "Big brother, can you help me?"
"What's up?"
"My mother was taken by some people, and they said if I wanted her back, I needed to tell you to follow me..."
Yuan fell silent.
"Please follow me, big brother.
I want my mother back..." the boy spoke again, looking like he was on the verge of bawling his eyes out.
"Alright, take me to them..." Yuan nodded a moment later.
Afterward, Yuan followed the boy for several blocks before they entered a narrow alleyway that ended in a dead end.
"So, where are these strangers and your mother?" Yuan asked without even bothering to look around.
However, the boy didn't respond.
Instead, he reached beneath his clothes, pulled out a dagger, and stabbed Yuan in the leg.
However, due to Yuan's physique, the boy lacked the strength to pierce his skin, much less injure him.
The boy's eyes widened in shock, and his body froze as his mind went blank, completely unsure of what to do next.
Yuan calmly turned his head to look at the boy and asked, "What are you doing?"
The boy dropped the knife and began walking back with a fearful expression on his face.
"Hey, where do you—"
Just as Yuan turned to follow him, a silhouette descended from above and landed behind him before thrusting a long blade made of Limitless into his back.
"This weapon has been infused with a poisonous Refined Crystal, so you'll be dead within a minute," the attacker said.
"However, if you answer my questions, I'll give you an antidote."
Yuan turned to face him, and the attacker was taken aback by how calm he looked.
"What question?" Yuan inquired.
"Are you Sergeant Yuan?"
"Indeed, I am."
"Thanks.
You can die now." The attacker chuckled.
"What about the antidote?"
"Did you really think I'd let you live?"
"No, not really."
The next moment, Yuan collapsed to the ground with a heavy thud.
Shortly afterward, the attacker rolled him onto his back and removed his mask before retrieving a device to take a picture of his face.
"And... sent," the attacker muttered after sending the evidence.
"It's been a while since we've had such an easy mission with such a high payout."
"I'd like to hear more about that."
A familiar voice suddenly resounded.
Startled, the attacker dropped the device and turned toward Yuan, who was slowly rising from the ground.
"I-Impossible!
How are you still alive?!" he exclaimed.
"Did you really think you could kill me with such weak poison?" Yuan responded with a cold smile.
"Weak?!
That wasn't just some ordinary poison!
It was one of the strongest poisons in the world!" the attacker revealed.
"If that's the case, then the poisons in this world are quite lacking," Yuan replied calmly.
"That said, I'm not surprised.
I don't see much need for poison in an environment like this."
"W-Who the hell are you...?"
"Hm?
Weren't you paying attention just now?
I already told you that I am Sergeant Yuan."

chapters.title: Chapter 2669 Interrogating the Attacker
paragraphs: "N-No! Something must have gone wrong, and the poison didn't apply properly!" The attacker muttered in disbelief. "Let's see if you'll survive this!"
The attacker shouted as he swung his sword,

Yuan didn't react and calmly stood still as the sword flew toward his neck, and a moment later, the sword decapitated him, sending his head spinning in the air before falling to the ground with a soft thud.
The attacker burst out laughing, "Hahaha! Bastard gave me a good scare! But he definitely won't be—"

The attacker halted his sentence as he choked on his own words, his eyes widening with shock and disbelief as Yuan's headless body moved with smooth and deliberate movements, bending down to pick up his own severed head like he was picking up a fallen hat.
Then, Yuan attached his own head back onto his neck, and the massive cut that split them began to regenerate, swiftly healing all damage until there wasn't even the slightest scar.
"You'll need to do more than sever my head to kill me," Yuan calmly said, breaking the silence.
"Y-Y-You fucking monster!" The attacker dropped his sword and turned to flee, completely forgetting that they were at a dead end and that there was nowhere to run.
"Why are you running? You haven't finished your mission yet."
Yuan slowly approached the attacker with a cold grin.
"G-Get away from me!" The attacker turned around and shouted.
"Huh?"
His terrified expression immediately became one full of confusion as Yuan's figure had suddenly vanished like a ghost.
"Did he leave?" he muttered aloud.
"Before I acquire what I want to know? Not a chance."

Yuan's voice suddenly resounded beside him, causing the attacker to turn to his right. However, the moment he caught a glimpse of Yuan's cold expression, he felt a hand clamp around his neck like the talons of an eagle.
"Let's go somewhere more quiet, shall we?"
Before the attacker could even comprehend the situation, the world around him abruptly turned pitch-black, as though he had been plunged into the deepest depths of the abyss.
"First question: who are you working for?" Yuan asked.
However, the attacker did not response, and he just realized where they were.
"T-This is the void?! Impossible! How can you use void control in the city?!"
"Wrong answer."
Yuan spoke coldly before partially withdrawing his protection from the man.
The next moment, the man screamed in agony as the void assaulted his right foot, devouring it until nothing remained.

But Yuan wasn't done. He continued withdrawing more and more of his protection, allowing the void to keep devouring the man so that he would feel every moment of it. Eventually, his entire right leg was gone.
"Still don't feel like answering? Let's work on the next leg—"
"W-W-Wait! I will answer! I work for the Angry Shadows!"
"Angry Shadows? What's that?"
"That's..."
When the man showed even the slightest hesitation, Yuan said nothing and removed the protection from the man's other foot, letting the void consume it.

"Ahhh!" the man screamed in agony before hurriedly answering, "The Angry Shadows are a group of professional assassins who specialize in killing people for money and valuables! We mainly operate within the Union!"
"Who hired you?" Yuan asked, despite already knowing the answer.
"I-I don't know! Our clients' privacy is our top priority, so we never ask for their identities! The only thing that matters is whether they can pay for the job!"
Yuan reached into the man's pocket, retrieved a device, and asked, "Is this how you contact the client?"
"Yes!"
Yuan tried to access it, but nothing happened.
"The device is encrypted! Only I can unlock it!"
Although Yuan could easily let the man access it for him, he decided to do something else.
'This device is protected by a formation... a level 6 formation... should be doable.'
He spent several minutes studying the formation hidden within the device before attempting to crack it.
After another three minutes, Yuan successfully cracked the formation, allowing him to access the device.
"What an ugly photo. Couldn't you have taken a better one?" Yuan shook his head after seeing the photo of his face that the man had sent to confirm his death.
"H-How?!" The man exclaimed in disbelief.
"Who gave you permission to ask questions?" Yuan coldly sneered before letting the void consume a few more inches of his leg.
After putting away the device, Yuan asked, "Now then... where is your hideout located?"
"I-I can't tell you that! I'll die!
Yuan frowned and said, "And you think you won't die to me if you don't answer?"
"Ahhh!"
Moments later, the man had his second leg completely devoured by the void.
"Still not answering?"
Yuan started letting the void consume the man's right hand.
"I-I'll tell you! I'll tell you!" The man screamed when half of his right arm was consumed.
"Our hideout is located at—"
Before the man could finish revealing the location, an intense pain interrupted him as the void began devouring his right arm again.
"W-Why?!"
The man asked when it stopped a few moments later.
"If you dare to try and lie to me again, I'll make sure you stay in here for an eternity."
The man's already pale complexion was drained of what little color remained.
'How can he tell that I was going to lie?!' he cried inwardly.
"Why aren't you speaking? Did you fall asleep? Want me to wake you up a little?"
"N-No! I am awake! And our hideout is at the Happy Pub in the Western District!"
"Happy Pub in the Western District, huh?" Yuan repeated. "See? That wasn't so difficult, was it?"
"Will you spare me now?" the man asked in a weak voice.
Yuan looked at him with a puzzled face.
"Spare you? Did I say that I'd let you live?"
"W-What?" The man stared at Yuan in stunned disbelief.
Without another word, Yuan left the void. The moment he did, the man left behind was completely devoured by it.

chapters.title: Chapter 2670 Angry Shadows
paragraphs: After emerging from the void, Yuan picked up the weapon left behind by the man and smiled, "Since it can be powered by Refined Ores, this must be a high-end weapon. To personally deliver me such an expensive gift... how nice of them."
After putting the sword away, Yuan wore his mask again and left the alley with the intention of visiting the Angry Shadows' hideout.
However, just as he exited the alley, he noticed the boy who had lured him standing not far away, as if waiting for someone.
"Waiting for your mother?" Yuan asked him.
The boy was startled to see Yuan standing before him.
"Y-You?! How are you still—?!" The boy hastily covered his own mouth when he realized that they were out in the open with pedestrians walking around.
Yuan leaned in and whispered, "How am I still alive? Why don't you guess?"
He showed the boy the weapon he'd just acquired.
When the boy saw the weapon, he immediately turned around and tried to flee, but Yuan grabbed him by the shoulder before he could take even two steps.
"H-Help! He's trying to kidnap me!" the boy immediately shouted, drawing the attention of those nearby.
Yuan smiled behind his mask and waved dismissively. "He's lying. He tried to pickpocket me just now."
The pedestrians turned their attention to the boy, and upon seeing his ragged clothes, immediately believed Yuan and continued on their way, paying the two of them no further attention.
"N-No! Please help!" the boy screamed desperately, but nobody even bothered to spare them a glance.
"If you cooperate with me, I promise I won't hurt you," Yuan said to him. "Or I can take you to the authorities and have them figure things out."
The moment the boy heard Yuan mention involving the authorities, he immediately fell silent.
"Good. Now follow me."
Yuan brought the boy back to the alley.
"How are you related to the Angry Shadows?" Yuan asked once they were at the dead end.
However, the boy was too busy examining the scene to respond.
"Where is that man's corpse? Didn't you kill him?" he asked.
"I am the one asking questions here," Yuan said in a stern voice.
The boy nodded and said, "I am... their lure."
"How long have you been working with them?"
"I just started..." When the boy met Yuan's cold gaze, he quickly added, "I swear! This was my first job, too!"
"How did you end up working for them?"
"How do you think? They promised me food and money if I worked for them, and as an orphan, it's my only chance of survival."
"Well, starting today, you will no longer be working for them."
"What?! Then how the hell am I supposed to survive?!" the boy shouted.
"There are plenty of options out there, and they're definitely better than working for criminals."
"Nobody will hire or help a young orphan like me!"

"You're just not looking hard enough or in the right places. In fact, I passed by a restaurant not far from here with a sign saying they were hiring waiters. Age didn't matter as long as you could carry dishes properly."
"That's..." The boy fell silent.
He was already well aware of that. In truth, he preferred working as a lure because it was low effort, and the pay was far better than what he could earn from an ordinary job.
"Anyway, regardless of your feelings, you have no choice but to find another job after today," Yuan suddenly said.
"Why is that?"
"Because the Angry Shadows will cease to exist after today."
"Alright. Take me to the Happy Pub," Yuan then said.
"You... can't be serious..."
"I'm dead serious."
After a moment of silence, the boy released a defeated sigh.
"Follow me..."
The boy led Yuan to the Western District, only about an hour's walk from their location. Then, after another fifteen minutes, they arrived at the Happy Pub.
"I thought you were going to destroy the Angry Shadows? What are we doing at a bar?" the boy asked Yuan.

The Happy Pub was a popular, well-known establishment throughout the Union, but aside from its core members, nobody knew it was the Angry Shadows' hideout. Naturally, even the boy had no idea and mistook Yuan's reason for bringing him there.
"You really didn't know this was the Angry Shadows' hideout?" Yuan looked at him and said.
"What!?" The boy exclaimed.
Yuan shook his head and sighed, "You can leave now, and don't come back."

The boy didn't question him and immediately left. However, instead of leaving entirely, he lingered at a distance—far enough to avoid getting caught up in whatever was about to happen, yet close enough to watch.
Meanwhile, Yuan entered the bar through the already-opened doors.

Inside, the establishment was laid out much like a restaurant, with tables spread throughout the room, but the atmosphere was anything but ordinary. It was a full-fledged bar, with loud music blaring and bright lights constantly flashing.
The place was also bustling with activity. Many of the tables were occupied by groups of beautiful women gathered around a single man, drinking and chatting merrily.
"Are you dining alone?" one of the waitresses asked as she approached Yuan shortly after he entered, dressed in a revealing black outfit with matching black pantyhose.
"Alone."
"Would you like to be seated outside, or do you want a private room?"
"Give me a private room."
"Very well. Please, follow me."
The waitress led Yuan to the back, where a hallway lined with several private rooms awaited them.

Once they were inside one of the rooms with the door closed, she asked, "Have you been here before? Do you have a specific girl in mind? If not, you can tell us your preferences. Of course, you can have multiple at once."
Yuan calmly looked at the waitress and said, "I do have someone in mind—the manager of this place. Bring them to me."
The waitress immediately froze, dumbfounded by his unexpected request, and simply stared at him in silence.
