Once they were inside one of the rooms with the door closed, she asked, "Have you been here before?
Do you have a specific girl in mind?
If not, you can tell us your preferences.
Of course, you can have multiple at once."
Yuan calmly looked at the waitress and said, "I do have someone in mind—the manager of this place.
Bring them to me."
The waitress immediately froze, dumbfounded by his unexpected request, and simply stared at him in silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 2671 Angry Shadows(2)
paragraphs: After a long, awkward moment of silence, the waitress finally snapped out of her daze and spoke, "S-Sorry, but can you repeat that? I think I misheard you just now."
Yuan calmly repeated, "Bring me your manager."
"I'm sorry, but the manager is not part of the—"
"I'm not here for pleasure. I have business with your manager. I don't like repeating myself because my hands get itchy, which makes me want to get violent, so hurry up."
"I-I understand... please give me a moment to speak with the manager." The waitress bowed to him before leaving in a hurry.
A few minutes later, the door to Yuan's private room opened, and several bulky, intimidating-looking men stepped inside.
Yuan calmly swept his gaze over the group and remarked sarcastically, "Are all of you managers here? One would've been enough."
Then, one of the men stepped forward and said, "You're not welcome at our establishment. You can either leave peacefully and in one piece, or leave in a body bag."
"What a drastic difference between those two choices." Yuan shook his head. "Also, I warned the waitress that if I had to repeat myself, I might have to get violent."
The men said nothing and exchanged glances before nodding in unison.
They turned their attention back to Yuan, and they started approaching him with aggressive movements.
Seeing this, Yuan immediately stood up and fought back. Even without using his cultivation, his superior physique alone was more than enough to deal with them.
"Agh!"
"How the hell are his punches so heavy?! It felt like I was struck by a spiked mace!"
With just a single punch from Yuan, the men were sent flying across the room, and in what felt like the blink of an eye, they were all lying on the cold floor, groaning in pain.
However, the men did not give up so easily. After taking a moment to steady themselves, they rose to their feet and reached for the weapons concealed beneath their clothes.
Yuan raised an eyebrow at the sight, though not because they had decided to resort to deadly force.
"Flip knives? Really?" Yuan muttered in surprise.
"You're dead meat, bastard!
"I'll fucking cut you into a hundred pieces!"
"I'll fucking cut you into a hundred pieces!"
The men shouted as they began closing in on Yuan with slow, cautious steps, clearly still wary of him.
However, they abruptly stopped in their tracks when Yuan drew his sword and casually waved it around like a magic wand.
"A-A high-grade weapon!"
When the men realized what Yuan was holding, they swiftly backed away until they were outside the room, then closed it.
"Q-Quick! Somebody go get the manager!"
"I'll go!"
"No, I'll go!"
Half of them began fighting for the role. Eventually, someone who wasn't part of the argument decided to go himself, leaving the others speechless.
While that man went to get the manager, the others stayed outside Yuan's door, just in case he wanted to leave.
Fortunately for them, Yuan had no intention of leaving and patiently stayed inside the room until a woman appeared a few minutes later.
"Is he still inside?" The woman asked the men stationed outside.
"Yes, he is."
"I'll be back."
"I'm coming in." The woman knocked on the door and announced her intent before entering.
Once inside, she could see Yuan calmly seated on one of the couches.
"I'm the manager of the Happy Pub. I heard you have some grievances with us. What is the issue, and how can we solve it?"
However, Yuan didn't respond and merely stared at her in silence.

Just as the woman opened her mouth again, Yuan retrieved his sword and stabbed it into the table before him. Then he examined the woman's reaction. If she was truly the manager of this place and related to the Angry Shadows, she'd recognize it.
However, the woman merely raised her eyebrows in a puzzled manner, looking like she was seeing the sword for the first time.

"I am trying to resolve your issue, and you're threatening me with a weapon? Do you really want to resolve it, or are you just here to cause trouble? If it's the latter, you can leave, or we'll call the authorities," said the woman a moment later.
"Are you the manager of this place?" Yuan then asked.
"That's right. And you called for me, no?"
Yuan narrowed his eyes at the woman, who did not appear to be lying.
"Unfortunately, you're not qualified to resolve my issue. Who is above you? The owner of this place?"
"Looks like I will have to get the authorities involved..." The woman sighed.
She turned around and prepared to leave, but halted when Yuan spoke, "Are you sure you want to do that? It might reveal the truth about this place."
"What nonsense are you spewing? There's nothing—"
"Angry Shadows..." Yuan muttered their name, and when the woman heard it, her expression changed drastically.
"Oh? Judging by your reaction, you are definitely connected to them. I was beginning to worry that I might have been fed the wrong information."
The woman did not respond. Instead, she silently approached Yuan and took a seat beside him.
Then, she placed a hand on his thigh and began gently caressing it.
"Esteemed guest, why don't we continue this conversation in my private chambers?" she said.
Yuan smiled and replied, "I'll consider it... if you show me what you're hiding in your other hand."
In response, the woman suddenly whipped out her other hand, which had been concealed within her outfit, and drove what appeared to be a needle straight into Yuan's thigh.

"I don't know how you obtained that information, but that's not something a stranger like you should be uttering!" the woman said coldly. "You've been poisoned. You have one minute to consume the antidote before the poison kills you, and if you want it, you'll answer my questions!
But instead of panicking as she expected, Yuan burst out laughing, leaving the woman speechless and bewildered.

chapters.title: Chapter 2672 Angry Shadows(3)
paragraphs: "W-What the hell is so funny?"
The woman questioned Yuan.

"You may find this hard to believe, but this isn't the first time I've heard something like that. In fact, someone told me the exact same thing right before I came here..." Yuan said, staring directly into the woman's eyes. "And do you know what happened to that man?"
The woman swallowed nervously, not daring to respond.
"Well, he died."
Yuan suddenly placed a hand on her shoulder, and before she could even react, the private room around them vanished, completely swallowed by the void.
"T-This is?!"
"We're in the void. If you answer my questions, I'll consider letting you out... alive."
To let the woman know that he wasn't joking, he allowed the void to consume the arm she had used to strike him just now.
"Ahhhh!"
The woman screamed in agony as she watched her own arm slowly being devoured by the void.
"First question... what's your connection with the Angry Shadows?" Yuan asked.
"B-Because of my connection to one of the members of Angry Shadows, I was given the role of managing the Happy Pub!"
"And what is that connection?"
"I am his wife!"
"Do you know any other member besides your husband?" Yuan then asked.
"No! I don't! I swear!"
'That explains why she doesn't recognize the sword...' Yuan thought to himself.
"How many members does the Angry Shadows have?"
"I don't know!"
"Then who in this place does?"
"Only the Angry Shadows would have such information! But none of them are at the Happy Pub currently!"
"When will they be here?"
"I don't know! It's completely random! They only show up whenever there's a meeting!"
Yuan pondered for a moment before speaking again.
"In that case... call your husband. As his wife, surely you have some way of contacting him, right?"
Yuan exited the void with the woman shortly after.
"Go ahead, contact your husband. If you don't want to go back to the void, that is."
The woman nodded and retrieved her phone to dial her husband.
"Hello? It's me—"
However, just as the call connected, Yuan snatched the phone from her and spoke into it, "Hey, are you this woman's husband?"
"Who the hell are you?"
"I'm her secret lover."
"What?! Listen here, you fucking—"
"We'll be waiting for you at the Happy Pub." Yuan interrupted the husband and hung up without warning.
"W-Why did you do that?!" the woman exclaimed in shock and disbelief.
Yuan did not answer. He merely gave her a cold stare, and she instantly fell silent.
While they waited for the husband to show up, the woman asked, "How are you still alive?"
Yuan remained silent.
Seeing that Yuan had no intention of speaking to her any further, the woman gave up trying to pry more information out of him and remained silent.
Eventually, the door burst open, and a rugged-looking man stormed into the room, his face flushed red with fury.
"Dear!" The woman immediately ran to his side.
"You dare cheat on me?!" the man roared, slapping her aside before she could even explain herself.
"I-It's not like that! He lied to lure you here!" she exclaimed from the floor, blood trickling from the corner of her lips.
Upon hearing this, the man finally regained his senses. It was only then that he noticed her missing arm.
"Y-Your arm! What happened to it?!" the man exclaimed, rushing to her side with a horrified expression.
The woman pointed at Yuan with her other hand and said, "He did it! He tortured me for information about the Angry Shadows! And somehow, he already knows this place is one of your hideouts!"
"What?!"
The man turned to look at Yuan with a deep frown on his face. At this moment, he finally noticed the sword resting on Yuan's lap.
"T-That sword! That's Second Shadow's sword! How did you—"
The man suddenly stopped speaking, realization dawning on his face.
"Your appearance... you must be Sergeant Yuan...
"Is Second Shadow—the owner of that sword still alive? Did you kill him?"
Yuan stood up and calmly approached the man.
"I will be the one asking questions here."
"Be careful! He can somehow use Void Control inside the city!"
"What?!"
Unfortunately, even with the woman's warning, there was nothing the man could do. A split second later, he and his wife were both dragged into the void by Yuan.
"This has to be an illusion! There's no way he can use Void Control inside the city, much less drag two people into the void with him!" the man exclaimed.
Yuan did not bother responding. Instead, he simply fed the woman's remaining arm to the void, his expression completely devoid of emotion.
"Ahhh!"
"Zing'er!" the man cried out, his complexion instantly paling at the sound of his wife's scream.
"How many members are there in Angry Shadows? If I don't receive an answer within five seconds, I'll take another one of her limbs."
"S-Six! There are six of us!"
"So five, huh?" Yuan remarked.
The man quietly gritted his teeth at Yuan's words, which had answered his earlier question about whether the sword's owner was still alive.
"Who ordered you to kill me?" Yuan asked.
"We don't know! We don't require our clients to reveal their identities. As long as they pay us, we'll accept anyone's request!"
Yuan already knew this from questioning the previous assassin and only wanted to confirm it.
"Can you summon the other four... No, I want you to summon the other four members to the Happy Pub. I don't care how you do it."
"That's—"
"One hour. I'll give you one hour. If all five of you are not gathered before me before that time, I'll kill this woman and level this entire building."
"You monster!"
"Pot calling the kettle black, huh? Had you not tried to kill me, I wouldn't be here."
Yuan took them out of the void the next moment.
Seeing that the man wasn't moving even after some time, Yuan spoke again. "You can stay here for as long as you want. Just know that this woman only has 57 minutes left to live."
Hearing this, the man snapped out of his daze and finally moved.

chapters.title: Chapter 2673 Angry Shadows(4)
paragraphs: After leaving the room, the man made his way to a secret room somewhere in the Happy Pub that was used exclusively by the Angry Shadows. Once there, he contacted the other members, revealing the situation to them.
"What?! Second Shadow was killed by Sergeant Yuan?! Are you certain about that, Sixth Shadow?!"

The man who had spoken with Yuan, known as Sixth Shadow in Angry Shadows, responded, "I'm almost certain. That bastard has Second Shadow's sword—a treasure he wouldn't part with even if his life depended on it."
"So, what does he want?"
"I don't know, but he wants to meet all of us," said Sixth Shadow.
"How ridiculous."
"Why the hell should we listen to such a demand?"
"Because he has my wife and threatened to kill her!"

After a moment of silence, one of the other members finally spoke. "Sixth Shadow, I'm sorry, but I'm not going to expose myself to someone so dangerous, even if your wife's life is on the line, and I expect everyone to do the same if I were in your shoes."
"Fifth Shadow is right. You should already know that the Angry Shadows come before everything—even family."
"This is exactly why I refuse to start a family... It's too risky and an unnecessary weakness."
"You'll be fine, Sixth Shadow. There are plenty of women out there. If you need help finding someone, I can have over a hundred women lined up for you by the end of the day!"
"As for this Sergeant Yuan... Let's just avoid him for now. I doubt he'll go out of his way to hunt all of us."
"We'll also refund the clients their money... the second payment, at least."
One by one, the other members of Angry Shadows disconnected the call, refusing to risk exposing themselves.

Sixth Shadow sat silently in the dimly lit room. Although he was devastated that the others had refused to comply with Yuan's demands to save his wife, it wasn't as though he hadn't expected this outcome.

In fact, he had already suspected things would turn out this way, which was why he hadn't even bothered trying to persuade them to change their minds. Moreover, if he had been in their shoes, he would have made the same decision.
Most importantly...
"There's no guarantee that he'd spare my wife..."
He looked at the time.
"Twenty-two minutes left, huh?"
After lingering for a few more minutes, Sixth Shadow stood up and left through a secret exit, disappearing not just from the room but from the Happy Pub entirely.
Time passed swiftly, and before long, the one-hour deadline came to an end. Yet, the Angry Shadows were nowhere to be seen, and even the woman's husband had failed to return.
"Looks like your husband has abandoned you," Yuan remarked, breaking the hour-long silence.
He turned to look at the woman when she offered no response, only to see that she didn't appear surprised at all, as if she'd anticipated this outcome.
"So you knew this would happen, huh?" he muttered.
"I knew this day would come the moment I agreed to marry him," she calmly replied.
"The Angry Shadows are the most infamous and secretive gang in the Union. There's no way they'd risk exposing themselves for a mere woman like me."
She turned to stare Yuan in the eyes and asked, "What are you going to do now? Spare me? Or kill me as you'd said?"
Yuan did not immediately respond.
He stood from his seat and walked to stand in front of her.
"Unfortunately, I rarely go back on my own words, especially when dealing with criminals," he said coldly. "Had you not tried to kill me, I would've probably spared you."
The woman let out a weak sigh, abandoning the last shred of hope she had left.
"Go ahead," she said as she closed her eyes.
Without a word, Yuan used Void Manipulation and tossed the woman into the void, ending her life in an instant.
"A pity," he mumbled.

At the end of the day, the woman was associated with criminals and had even tried to kill him, so Yuan felt no guilt over taking her life. Moreover, if he had spared her after making his threat, the Angry Shadows would no longer take him seriously, as his words would have lost all weight in their eyes.
"What now?"
Instead of leaving, Yuan lingered in the room for a little longer to ponder his next steps. He had wanted to acquire more evidence on the Gu Family before returning, but that was no longer possible.
"At the very least, I still have this..."

Yuan retrieved the device Second Shadow had left behind, which proved that the Angry Shadows had indeed been hired to kill him. However, it did not directly implicate the Gu Family, as there was nothing on the device that could identify them as the ones who had issued the request.
"No... wait a second... As long as the Angry Shadows hasn't told them that I survived, I might be able to use this to lure them out..."
Upon realizing this, Yuan immediately left the Happy Pub and made his way back to the Central District.
To evade detection by the Gu Family, Yuan bought new clothes and a mask that completely changed his disguise before returning.
Once he returned to the Central District, Yuan went straight to the Supreme General's living quarters and knocked on the door.
The Supreme General answered the door a few moments later and stared at Yuan with a suspicious gaze.
"It's me, Sergeant Yuan," Yuan said.
"I can tell who you are even with that getup. Did you just get back from wandering around the city? What do you want from me?"
"Can I come inside?"
"No." The Supreme General immediately refused.
"I was nearly assassinated while I was outside the city," Yuan swiftly revealed without hesitation.
The Supreme General raised an eyebrow at his words. After a brief moment of silence, he stepped aside and said, "Come in."

Most importantly...
"There's no guarantee that he'd spare my wife..."
He looked at the time.
"Twenty-two minutes left, huh?"
After lingering for a few more minutes, Sixth Shadow stood up and left through a secret exit, disappearing not just from the room but from the Happy Pub entirely.
Time passed swiftly, and before long, the one-hour deadline came to an end.
Yet, the Angry Shadows were nowhere to be seen, and even the woman's husband had failed to return.
"Looks like your husband has abandoned you," Yuan remarked, breaking the hour-long silence.
He turned to look at the woman when she offered no response, only to see that she didn't appear surprised at all, as if she'd anticipated this outcome.
"So you knew this would happen, huh?" he muttered.
"I knew this day would come the moment I agreed to marry him," she calmly replied.
"The Angry Shadows are the most infamous and secretive gang in the Union.
There's no way they'd risk exposing themselves for a mere woman like me."
She turned to stare Yuan in the eyes and asked, "What are you going to do now?
Spare me?
Or kill me as you'd said?"
Yuan did not immediately respond.
He stood from his seat and walked to stand in front of her.
"Unfortunately, I rarely go back on my own words, especially when dealing with criminals," he said coldly.
"Had you not tried to kill me, I would've probably spared you."
The woman let out a weak sigh, abandoning the last shred of hope she had left.
"Go ahead," she said as she closed her eyes.
Without a word, Yuan used Void Manipulation and tossed the woman into the void, ending her life in an instant.
"A pity," he mumbled.
At the end of the day, the woman was associated with criminals and had even tried to kill him, so Yuan felt no guilt over taking her life.
Moreover, if he had spared her after making his threat, the Angry Shadows would no longer take him seriously, as his words would have lost all weight in their eyes.
"What now?"
Instead of leaving, Yuan lingered in the room for a little longer to ponder his next steps.
He had wanted to acquire more evidence on the Gu Family before returning, but that was no longer possible.
"At the very least, I still have this..."
Yuan retrieved the device Second Shadow had left behind, which proved that the Angry Shadows had indeed been hired to kill him.
However, it did not directly implicate the Gu Family, as there was nothing on the device that could identify them as the ones who had issued the request.
"No... wait a second...
As long as the Angry Shadows hasn't told them that I survived, I might be able to use this to lure them out..."
Upon realizing this, Yuan immediately left the Happy Pub and made his way back to the Central District.
To evade detection by the Gu Family, Yuan bought new clothes and a mask that completely changed his disguise before returning.
Once he returned to the Central District, Yuan went straight to the Supreme General's living quarters and knocked on the door.
The Supreme General answered the door a few moments later and stared at Yuan with a suspicious gaze.
"It's me, Sergeant Yuan," Yuan said.
"I can tell who you are even with that getup.
Did you just get back from wandering around the city?
What do you want from me?"
"Can I come inside?"
"No." The Supreme General immediately refused.
"I was nearly assassinated while I was outside the city," Yuan swiftly revealed without hesitation.
The Supreme General raised an eyebrow at his words.
After a brief moment of silence, he stepped aside and said, "Come in."

chapters.title: Chapter 2674 Request Canceled
paragraphs: Once Yuan entered the Supreme General's living quarters, the latter closed the door behind him and said, "Start from the beginning."
Yuan nodded and recounted everything that had happened while he was outside the city, omitting a few details, such as his use of Void Manipulation to interrogate the offenders.
He then placed the device he acquired from Second Shadow onto the table.
"This is evidence that I was targeted."
The Supreme General picked up the device and looked through the evidence, raising an eyebrow when he saw the photo Second Shadow used to prove Yuan's death.
"How does this photo of you prove your death? It looks like you're just sleeping to me," said the Supreme General.
"They tried to poison me."
"If that's true, how did you survive the poison? Don't tell me that you always walk around with antidotes or something?"
Yuan smiled and said, "Of course not. My body is naturally resilient to poison."
The Supreme General did not doubt him because he was already confirmed to have the Perfected Heavenly Refinement physique.

After going through all of the evidence, the Supreme General put the device back down and said, "You're right. There isn't any evidence in here that can identify the ones who paid for your assassination."
"What if I say that I already know who they are?" Yuan asked.
"Are you going to say it was the Gu Family?" the Supreme General asked calmly, as though he were already aware of the situation.
"So you already knew, huh?"
"There's nothing that happens within my military that I don't know about," he sneered.
"So you already knew, huh?"
"There's nothing that happens within my military that I don't know about," he sneered.
"Then why haven't you done anything? Is it because you're suspicious of me?" Yuan asked.

The Supreme General narrowed his eyes at him and replied, "It has nothing to do with you. There are rules that must be followed, and unless we can prove beyond a shadow of a doubt that they're guilty, there's nothing we can do, even if we are convinced of their guilt."
"Doesn't that just enable people to deliberately exploit the loophole?" Yuan asked, shaking his head.
"I won't comment any further on the military's rules, since they were established long before I came into power," the Supreme General said.
"So I just need evidence, right? I plan on using this device to do so."
"If you intend to use it to lure them out, it won't work. They can simply turn it around and use it as a defense instead. It's called entrapment, and there have been precedents for that as well."
Yuan was speechless at this point.
"So you're telling me to just sit around and wait until they successfully kill me after countless attempts because nobody can prove it's them. Sometimes, such rules only benefit the powerful."
"Or, you can catch them in the act and find evidence—"
"Not everyone has the time for that." Yuan interrupted.
After saying that, Yuan turned around and walked to the exit.
"What are you going to do?" The Supreme General asked.
"Why bother asking when there appears to be nothing that I can do?"
"You—"
Yuan left before the Supreme General could finish his sentence.
Then, he made his way to the living quarters the Gu Family were staying in and knocked on their door.
A moment later, Colonel Gu answered the door, and his face immediately twisted with shock and disbelief upon seeing Yuan's face.
"You look like you've just seen a ghost," Yuan remarked.
"W-Why are you here?" Colonel Gu had to swallow forcefully before speaking.
Yuan smiled and replied, "I just wanted to tell you that I have given General Gu plenty of chances. Unfortunately, he is clearly determined to see me dead."
"What the hell are you talking about? General Gu wants you dead? Do you have any evidence to support such outrageous accusations?" Colonel Gu frowned.

"Evidence this, evidence that. Every time you want to avoid the consequences, you hide behind that word like it's some kind of get-out-of-jail-free card. Someone who's truly innocent wouldn't rely on it so desperately."
"Is that all you have to say? If so, you can leave now.
The smile on Yuan's face became colder, even a little sinister, but he didn't say anything else and turned around and walked away.
The Supreme General, who watched their interaction from the window, sighed in relief when Yuan left peacefully, as he was fully prepared to intervene if Yuan had attacked Colonel Gu.
Meanwhile, once Colonel Gu closed the door and went back inside the house, he snapped.
"WHAT THE HELL IS GOING ON?! WHY IS THAT BASTARD STILL ALIVE?!?!"
Major Gu, who was inside his room, came out after hearing the commotion and asked, "What happened?"
Colonel Gu gritted his teeth angrily and explained, "We've been lied to again!"
"Don't tell me..." Major Gu swallowed nervously.
"That's right! That bastard is still alive, even though the Angry Shadows presented proof of his 'death' earlier today!"
"Those fucking scammers!"
After a moment of silence, Major Gu asked, "What should we do now? Should we stop—"

"Stop?!" Colonel Gu snapped. "Our best chance to get rid of him is while he's still in the Union! If we can't even eliminate a single bastard, the General will start questioning our competence—and whether we're worth keeping around!"
Major Gu trembled at such words.

Colonel Gu began biting his nails as he muttered, "Fuck... I wanted to get rid of him without getting our own hands dirty, but that doesn't seem possible if even the Angry Shadows, the most reputable gang in this place, are scamming us."
However, just as he spoke those words, Major Gu received a message.
"T-The Angry Shadows has just refunded our second payment! Three hundred million credits!" Major Gu exclaimed after seeing it.
"What?" Colonel Gu frowned.
"Did they give a reason?"
Major Gu read the rest of the message and swallowed nervously before replying, "They said it's because they're canceling our request... and they didn't give a proper reason for it."
"What the hell is going on?! None of this makes sense!" Colonel Gu pinched the bridge of his nose, completely stressed out by the puzzling situation.

chapters.title: Chapter 2675 Colonel Gu's Assassination Attempt
paragraphs: "So let me get this straight... Sergeant Yuan is still alive, not because the Angry Shadows scammed us, but because they canceled our request... after they sent evidence of his death to us?" Colonel Gu felt a headaching approaching as he tried to figure out the situation.
If the Angry Shadows had really intended to scam them, they wouldn't have refunded the three hundred million credits.
However, the most puzzling part was why the Angry Shadows had sent them evidence of Yuan's death before canceling the request.
"They probably realized that their scam was too obvious, so they decided to cancel the request altogether to save their own reputation," Major Gu revealed his assumption about the situation.
Colonel Gu closed his eyes and took several deep breaths before speaking, "Forget it. It doesn't matter anymore since they have canceled our request and refunded our money."
"What do we do now? We don't have enough time to hire another gang, either."
"As I said earlier, I'll personally take care of him. It's a little risky, but I am going to kill him tonight," said Colonel Gu.
"You're going to do it tonight?! That's more than a little risky! I doubt he'll be going out again, so you'll have to assassinate him inside his own residence!" Major Gu exclaimed in disbelief.
"That's exactly what I intend to do. It's such an outrageous and reckless move that no one would suspect us. Even if they do, they won't have any evidence—I will make sure of it."
"Do you need my help? Or are you going to do this alone?" Major Gu asked.
"I work better alone."
"Alright."
Time passed swiftly, and before they knew it, the sky had grown completely dark.
Two hours past midnight, Colonel Gu quietly slipped out of his residence in disguise, carrying a certain treasure with him.

Although it was late at night, several servants were still stationed outside. Yet not a single one noticed Colonel Gu or sensed his presence as he made his way toward Yuan's residence, which was only a minute away.
'General Gu was truly a genius for lending me this treasure...' Colonel Gu thought with a smile.
After reaching Yuan's residence, he quietly checked the windows one by one to see if any had been left unlocked. Sure enough, he eventually found one, allowing him to slip inside with ease.
Upon entering Yuan's living quarters, Colonel Gu tried to sense his presence. When he failed to detect anything, he began searching the rooms one by one.
Some time later—
"What the hell? He's not home?" Colonel Gu was dumbfounded when he realized that Yuan wasn't actually at home.
'This isn't possible! We kept an eye on his residence throughout the entire day and never saw him leave!'
Colonel Gu checked the residence again, and sure enough, Yuan was nowhere to be seen.
"Where the hell is he?!"
Although he considered leaving, Colonel Gu was reluctant to let all his efforts go to waste, so he decided to linger for a while longer, hoping Yuan would return soon.
Meanwhile, Major Gu patiently waited for Colonel Gu's return, sipping tea as he sat on a couch in the living room.
Suddenly, he sensed a presence nearby.
"Huh? You're back already?" Major Gu called out as he turned toward the door.
But no one was there.
"Was I just imagining things?" he muttered before returning his attention to the book in his hands.
A few moments later, he sensed the presence again, but this time, it was directly behind him.
A chill ran down Major Gu's spine as he whipped his head around so abruptly that some of the tea spilled from his cup.
Unsurprisingly, there was nobody behind him when he looked.
"Fuck... what is going on? Am I feeling paranoid because of Colonel Gu's risky mission?" he sighed.
However, as time passed, Major Gu kept sensing the mysterious presence appear and disappear around him several times, almost as if a ghost was provoking him.
"Colonel, stop messing with me!" Major Gu eventually had enough and shouted angrily. "The General didn't give you that treasure so you could play around with it!"
He was convinced that Colonel Gu had returned and was messing with him, using the treasure General Gu had given him in case they needed to dirty their own hands.
After a moment of silence, a calm voice resounded.
"You caught me."
However, Major Gu immediately jumped at the sound of the voice, his heart jolting with alarm.
It wasn't Colonel Gu's voice, but it was a familiar one!
He immediately began looking around in a panic, but no matter how hard he searched, he couldn't find the source of the voice.
"Show yourself, you bastard!" Major Gu cried out loud.
Suddenly, he sensed the presence again—this time, directly behind him.
Major Gu whipped his head around, but just as he caught a glimpse of someone's face, the figure reached out and clamped a hand over his neck.
"S-Sergeant Yuan?! What are you—" Major Gu muttered in disbelief as he stared at Yuan's handsome face.
However, Yuan didn't say anything and directly activated Void Manipulation, entering the void with Major Gu in tow.
"?!?!?" Major Gu's eyes widened with shock and disbelief at Yuan using Void Manipulation.
"Void Control?! That's impossible!"
Just like Gaia's Heaven, the Union was protected by a formation that suppressed everyone's cultivation, naturally making it impossible to use techniques such as Void Control within its boundaries.
Yet, for some reason, Yuan was able to bypass that restriction.
"Don't tell me you can also—"
Yuan suddenly tightened his grip, nearly crushing Major Gu's windpipe.
"Do you think you'll get away with this?!" Major Gu forced out with great difficulty.
Despite the dire situation he was in, he did not truly believe Yuan would dare to kill him.
"Go ahead and kill me if you dare! Gaia's System will brand you as a traitor for killing a fellow soldier!" Major Gu was so confident that he even dared to provoke Yuan.

A cold grin appeared on Yuan's face as he replied, "I already asked Ironwoman about how the system works. According to her, it doesn't directly know what you do. Instead, it senses your killing intent. If you direct that killing intent toward another soldier and the system loses its connection to that soldier shortly afterward, it concludes that you were the one who killed them, or were somehow related."

"Of course, it can also sense when you make physical contact with someone also with Gaia's System. But if that's how the system works, then the solution is simple. I just need to kill you without touching you or directing any killing intent toward you."
Major Gu's eyes widened at Yuan's words.

Although Yuan made it sound simple, killing someone without leaking even the slightest trace of killing intent was practically impossible. It went against human nature, and even the most experienced killers would struggle to completely suppress their killing intent when targeting someone.

That said, such logic only applied to the people of this world. With Yuan's vast experience and the countless lives he had taken, suppressing his killing intent completely was well within his capabilities.
"E-Even if that's true, do you really dare to risk it?! What if Ironwoman was wrong?" Major Gu asked nervously.
After seeing the resolve in Yuan's eyes, his earlier confidence had already begun to crumble.
"If Ironwoman was wrong and I end up being branded a traitor... well, I'll deal with it when the time comes," Yuan replied nonchalantly, as though he couldn't care less about the consequences.
"You can't be serious!"
However, the cold resolve in Yuan's eyes told Major Gu otherwise. He was completely serious.
"Wait! I'll tell General Gu to stop targeting you!" Major Gu suddenly blurted out, desperation filling his eyes.
Yuan narrowed his eyes and sneered coldly. "We're already far beyond that point. I gave you plenty of warnings and more than enough chances to back off, but alas, you just couldn't help yourselves."

Yuan released his grip on Major Gu and said, "I won't kill you immediately, so enjoy what little time you have left in the void. Use it to reflect on all the crimes you've committed throughout your life."
"W-Wait! No! Come back! We can talk about this!" Major Gu screamed like a pig being led to the slaughterhouse as he watched Yuan leave the void, abandoning him alone in the endless abyss.
However, Yuan completely ignored his pleas and left the void without looking back.
Once he returned to the room, Yuan waited until Colonel Gu left his residence before making his own way back.

Although he could have dealt with Colonel Gu as well, having both of them disappear in a single night would have been far too suspicious. Moreover, Yuan wanted to instill fear in the Gu Family by slowly crushing them one by one.
When Colonel Gu returned to his residence, he shouted in frustration, "Fuck! That bastard wasn't home! Where the hell did he disappear to?!"
He expected Major Gu to respond, but no answer came.
"Gu Ming?" he called out.
"Did he fall asleep?"
Colonel Gu headed to Major Gu's bedroom, only to find it empty. He searched the entire residence, calling his name repeatedly, but to no avail.'
"Where the hell did he go while knowing that I was out on such an important mission?!"
It was as though Major Gu had vanished without a trace.

With no choice but to wait for his return, Colonel Gu sat on the couch in the living room for the rest of the night, completely unaware that Major Gu was trapped within the void in that very same room.

However, Yuan completely ignored his pleas and left the void without looking back.
Once he returned to the room, Yuan waited until Colonel Gu left his residence before making his own way back.
Although he could have dealt with Colonel Gu as well, having both of them disappear in a single night would have been far too suspicious.
Moreover, Yuan wanted to instill fear in the Gu Family by slowly crushing them one by one.
When Colonel Gu returned to his residence, he shouted in frustration, "Fuck!
That bastard wasn't home!
Where the hell did he disappear to?!"
He expected Major Gu to respond, but no answer came.
"Gu Ming?" he called out.
"Did he fall asleep?"
Colonel Gu headed to Major Gu's bedroom, only to find it empty.
He searched the entire residence, calling his name repeatedly, but to no avail.'
"Where the hell did he go while knowing that I was out on such an important mission?!"
It was as though Major Gu had vanished without a trace.

With no choice but to wait for his return, Colonel Gu sat on the couch in the living room for the rest of the night, completely unaware that Major Gu was trapped within the void in that very same room.

chapters.title: Chapter 2676 Major Gu's Disappearance
paragraphs: "Where the hell is that idiot?!" Colonel Gu muttered irritably. He had waited the entire night for Major Gu to return, yet there was still no sign of him.
As much as he wanted to continue waiting, Colonel Gu had no choice but to leave, as the Supreme General had summoned everyone for a brief meeting before the assembly.
Later that afternoon, everyone from Gaia's Heaven gathered as instructed—with one exception.
"Where's Major Gu?" The Supreme General questioned when he noticed Major Gu's absence.
"I don't know." Colonel Gu shook his head.
"What?" The Supreme General frowned. "You don't know where your roommate went?"
"He left without saying a word." Colonel Gu shrugged.
"Whatever. This is just a brief meeting to let you all know that the assembly will begin tomorrow. We'll gather here again at 0800 sharp, and I expect everyone to be here."
"Yes, Supreme General."
"Dismissed."
After being dismissed, Colonel Gu subconsciously glanced at Yuan, only for his eyes to widen when he realized Yuan was also staring back at him.
A cold, sinister smile hung on Yuan's face, sending a chill down Colonel Gu's spine.
When Colonel Gu saw Yuan's smile, an ominous feeling washed over him, though he couldn't understand why. Nor did he make any connection between Yuan and Major Gu's disappearance.
Once Colonel Gu returned to his residence, he tried calling Major Gu for the umpteenth time. However, just like before, the call went straight to voicemail.
"This doesn't make sense! Why would his phone be off? He never turns off his—"
Colonel Gu suddenly froze mid-sentence as a look of realization flashed across his face. Then, Yuan's face surfaced in Colonel Gu's mind, along with the cold, sinister smile he had worn earlier.
"That bastard! It can't be!"
Colonel Gu finally connected the dots, but he still couldn't bring himself to believe it.
"Don't tell me the reason he wasn't home last night was that he was here!"
Although he was almost certain Yuan had something to do with Major Gu's disappearance, he couldn't fathom how he had managed to make him vanish without leaving behind a single trace.
"There wasn't even the slightest sign of a struggle... Did Gu Ming leave with him willingly?
Unfortunately, there was only one way to get the answers he wanted, so Colonel Gu begrudgingly made his way to Yuan's residence to confront him directly.
BANG! BANG! BANG!
Colonel Gu pounded on the door like a desperate loan shark collecting on a debt that meant life or death.
"I know you're in there! Come out!"
BANG! BANG! BANG!
When several moments passed and Yuan didn't answer, Colonel Gu kept knocking, using so much force that he loosened the hinges.
"Sergeant Yuan! Come out, you bastard!"
BANG! BANG! BANG!
Just as Colonel Gu was on the verge of breaking down the door, a stern voice resounded behind him.
"What do you think you're doing, Colonel Gu?!"
It was a woman's voice.
"Get lost! This is none of your business!" Colonel Gu snapped without even turning around, already recognizing Ironwoman from her voice alone.
"Oh? Are you telling me to get lost?"
A second voice suddenly sounded from behind him, causing Colonel Gu's body to visibly stiffen.
He slowly turned around and saw not only Ironwoman standing there, but the Supreme General as well.
"N-No... that's—"
"What business do you have with Sergeant Yuan?" The Ironwoman interrupted him.
Colonel Gu opened his mouth, but no words came out, as he had no idea how to explain the situation.

Suddenly, the door behind him creaked open, and Yuan appeared before them. He was half-naked, as though he had just stepped out of the shower. Water still glistened across his body, and his hair was damp.
The Ironwoman's eyes widened at the sight. Meanwhile, the Supreme General raised an eyebrow.
"What's with all the commotion? I was taking a bath, so I couldn't answer the door," Yuan said.
He glanced at the damaged door, then at Colonel Gu, before continuing, "You were the one knocking just now, right? With how urgently you were pounding on the door, one might think someone had died."
When Colonel Gu heard Yuan's last few words, his face flushed with redness.
"You! Where is Major Gu?! Where did you take him?!"
Yuan raised an eyebrow, looking genuinely puzzled as he responded, "Major Gu? What are you talking about? Why would I know where he is? And you're making it sound like I kidnapped him or something."
"Explain yourself, Colonel Gu," the Supreme General suddenly demanded.
"I don't know what is going on either! All I know is that Major Gu has been missing since last night, and I believe he has the answers!" Colonel Gu exclaimed, pointing directly at Yuan.
The Supreme General turned to look at Yuan, who was pointing at himself with a bewildered expression.

He then spoke, "Like I said earlier, why would I know anything about Major Gu's whereabouts? He's been missing since last night, right? Well, I've been home ever since I returned from wandering around the city."
"You're lying! After all, I—"
Colonel Gu abruptly stopped himself, cold sweat breaking out across his back as he realized he had nearly exposed himself.
He knew Yuan was lying about being home the entire time because he had personally sneaked into his residence the previous night. However, he couldn't reveal that without exposing his own actions.
"I'm lying?" Yuan repeated Colonel Gu's words with a frown. "Do you have evidence? Or are you just spewing bullshit for whatever reason?"
"You!"
Colonel Gu finally snapped and suddenly lunged for Yuan's neck.
However, before his hand could reach him, the tip of a sword appeared at Colonel Gu's own throat, halting his movements.
Once he froze in place, Colonel Gu caught sight of one of the Midnight Squad members standing beside him from the corner of his eye, a sword in their grasp—the same one currently pointed at his neck.
"You dare attack another soldier in my presence?!" the Supreme General roared, his voice cold and trembling with barely restrained anger.
He continued, "Withdraw your hand immediately! If it moves even a millimeter closer to Sergeant Yuan, I'll have it severed!"

chapters.title: Chapter 2677 Major Gu's Disappearance(2)
paragraphs: After hearing the Supreme General's words, Colonel Gu slowly withdrew his arm from Yuan.
"I apologize for my behavior just now. I acted without thinking," he said.
Yuan then spoke. "I don't know what your problem is, but I truly have no idea where Major Gu is."
"Are you sure you're not misunderstanding something?" Ironwoman remarked.
Colonel Gu took a deep breath before replying, "No, you're right. It must have been a misunderstanding. My mistake."
"You should be saying that to Sergeant Yuan."
Colonel Gu clenched his hands into tight fists as he looked at Yuan and forced out the words through gritted teeth.
"It was my mistake. I'm sorry."
"Everyone makes mistakes, so I'll forgive you. Just make sure it doesn't happen again," Yuan said.
"Anyway, now that things are resolved, I'm going to return to my bath."
"Ahem!" The Supreme General loudly cleared his throat before speaking, "Meet me at my residence once you are done. I need to have a word with you."
"Sure."
Afterward, everyone returned to their own residence.
"That bastard is definitely behind Gu Ming's disappearance!"
Although Colonel Gu had lost a great deal of face just now, at least he had managed to confirm his suspicions about Yuan's involvement in Major Gu's disappearance.
A moment later, he pulled out his phone and contacted General Gu, seeking advice on how he should proceed.
Meanwhile, Yuan went to meet with the Supreme General.
However, when he arrived, the Supreme General wasn't alone, as the Midnight Squad was also present.
"I'll get straight to the point. Are you involved with Major Gu's disappearance?" the Supreme General questioned as soon as the door closed.
"What makes you think I am?" Yuan asked.

"That doesn't answer my question. I'll ask you again. Are you involved in Major Gu's disappearance in any way? If the next words out of your mouth aren't the truth, I'll have you cut down where you stand."
The Supreme General's voice was harsh, and the severity in his gaze made it clear that he was completely serious.
After a moment of silence, Yuan sighed before responding clearly, "No, I am not involved with Major Gu's disappearance."
The Supreme General's eyes widened slightly at Yuan's response, as though he couldn't believe what he was hearing.
"Even though you clearly have a motive?"

Yuan narrowed his eyes and replied in a disappointed tone, "I can understand why Colonel Gu would suspect me, but for you to believe I had something to do with Major Gu's disappearance as well? I'm starting to wonder if you're actually on General Gu's side."
Hearing Yuan's words, the Supreme General abruptly slammed his fist into the table beside him, splitting it in half.
"Don't you dare utter such nonsense before me again! I'd rather be dead than side with that slimeball!"
"Can you really blame me for thinking that with how you're treating me right now?" Yuan shrugged.

The Supreme General rubbed the bridge of his nose for a moment before speaking again, "Let's get back onto the topic. So you claim that you have nothing to do with Major Gu's disappearance, is that correct?"
"That is correct."
"Are you willing to swear on it?"
"I swear on my adoptive parents that I'm telling the truth. If I'm lying, may the heavens strike them dead!"
"Fine. You may leave."
"Do you believe me?"
"No, not really. However, I don't have evidence."
"And you won't find any. Because I really have nothing to do with Major Gu's disappearance."
The Supreme General didn't respond and merely gestured for him to leave.
"See you tomorrow," said Yuan as he walked out the door.
Once Yuan was gone, the Supreme General spoke aloud. "What do you think? Do you believe him?"
The next moment, Ironwoman emerged from one of the nearby rooms, having listened to the entire conversation.
"It's certainly difficult to believe him, especially given the circumstances. As for what I personally think... I believe in him—as a person."
"Quite a specific choice of words..." the Supreme General remarked, narrowing his eyes at her.
"If you don't believe him, why did you let him walk?" she then asked.
"Because I don't have any evidence against him," he said with a nonchalant shrug. "Even if I am convinced he did it, as long as I don't have solid evidence, I cannot touch him."
Ironwoman shook her head and sighed. "This is exactly why some people call you the Law-Abiding Fanatic."
"If I, as the Supreme General, don't follow the rules and regulations, then who will? I have to set an example, regardless of who it inconveniences or benefits."
"And yet here we are, with General Gu and countless others taking advantage of that very principle."
"Nobody can hide forever, and the moment I catch them..." The Supreme General muttered, purposefully leaving his sentence unfinished.
Time passed swiftly, and in the blink of an eye, it was 0800 the following morning. Everyone gathered as instructed, ready to attend the assembly.
Everyone, of course, except Major Gu, who was still nowhere to be found.
"I take it Major Gu still hasn't returned?" the Supreme General asked Colonel Gu.
"No..." Colonel Gu replied, slowly shaking his head.
"If he doesn't return by the time we are done with the assembly, I will send a search squad to look for him."
"Yes, Supreme General."

Although the Supreme General did not fully believe Yuan, he also couldn't dismiss the possibility that Major Gu had deliberately disappeared on his own to frame Yuan, giving General Gu even more ammunition to use against him.
That being said, unless Major Gu was prepared to remain hidden for a long time or abandon his identity entirely, such a possibility seemed unlikely.
A few moments later, one of the servants approached them and asked, "Are we prepared to head to the assembly?"
The Supreme General nodded. "We're ready."
"Then allow me to guide you there."
With that, the servant began leading them toward the massive white building in the distance, which had loomed on the horizon ever since their arrival in the Central District.

chapters.title: Chapter 2678 The Assembly
paragraphs: As they approached the white building in the distance, Yuan glanced at Ironwoman as he noticed that her hair was a different color than usual.
Noticing Yuan's gaze, Ironwoman turned to look at him, and that's when Yuan noticed that her eyes had also changed color.
"Are you wondering about my disguise?" she asked.
"Somewhat, but I can already guess why."
"Oh? You can? Let's hear it."
Yuan shrugged and revealed his thoughts.

"There's only one reason anyone disguises themselves—to hide their true identity. And considering you're going out of your way to enhance your disguise when you already wear a mask all the time, I can only assume there's someone at the assembly who might recognize you, and you're trying to prevent that."
The Ironwoman fell silent at his words.
"Did I get it wrong?" Yuan asked.
"I'm not telling you," she replied.
Yuan smiled and didn't pursue the matter further.

But that was not the end of the conversation, as the Supreme General suddenly turned to look at Yuan and asked, "And why are you wearing a mask? Are you also trying to hide your identity from someone in the assembly?"
"I don't want to disrupt the assembly with my handsome face," he joked, leaving both the Supreme General and Ironwoman speechless.
Of course, Ironwoman was well aware of the real reason Yuan was hiding his face—that he was actually the main subject of the assembly.
One would expect the Ironwoman or General Mei to reveal this information to the Supreme General before the assembly, but they kept it to themselves.
It wasn't that they didn't trust the Supreme General, either. They simply decided to let Yuan handle it all by himself.
"We have arrived," the servant announced as they reached the gate.
When it opened, a single path was revealed, lined with flowers on both sides and leading toward another gate at the entrance of the massive white building.
Although they couldn't see them from where they stood, eight other similar paths surrounded the building, each designated for a different city.
The servant continued leading Yuan and the others into the building. Inside, they were greeted by a grand hallway adorned with paintings and other works of art.
Although they couldn't see them from where they stood, eight other similar paths surrounded the building, each designated for a different city.
The servant continued leading Yuan and the others into the building. Inside, they were greeted by a grand hallway adorned with paintings and other works of art.
At the end of the hallway stood a large door that opened into a spacious white chamber with a massive circular table at its center.
Nine seats were arranged around the table, each marked with a distinct flag representing one of the nine cities.
Just as the representatives of Gaia's Heaven stepped into the room, the representatives from the other eight cities entered as well.
Without exchanging a word, the highest-ranking authority from each group made their way to the table and took their seats, while everyone else remained standing along the walls.
Once all of the seats were occupied, a tenth individual stepped forward and spoke loudly, "Gaia's Heaven."
"Present," the Supreme General said aloud.
"Spirit City."
"Present."
The man continued calling out every single city one by one.
"Ember City... Eastern Dawn... Mirage City... Rising Sun... Cloudpiercer... Jade City... Heavenly Furnace..."
"Present."
Once all nine cities had been called and accounted for, the man announced, "The assembly will now begin."
However, a long moment passed, and nobody spoke. Instead, eight of the nine people at the table turned their attention to the representative from Ember City, the one who had called the assembly.
The representative from Ember City cleared his throat before speaking.

"I called for this assembly for one reason—to talk about a new enemy that may pose a serious threat to humanity. I'm sure you've all heard the rumors by now, but we recently discovered a new type of Void Specter... one capable of perfectly disguising itself as a human."
No one responded or showed any surprise upon hearing this, as they had all already learned about it through the investigation not long ago.
"I will now allow the soldiers who encountered this Void Specter, which we have nicknamed the Impersonator, to recount their experience."
At his gesture, several soldiers stepped forward.
Yuan raised an eyebrow when he recognized them. They were the same soldiers he had encountered in the Black Zone.
"My name is..."
The soldiers introduced themselves before recounting their encounter with Yuan.
"We were carrying out a mission in the Black Zone when we came across what appeared to be a lone, lost soldier. At first, we thought he might need help, so we approached him."

"However, the moment we got close, he suddenly attacked us and killed one of our men. We fought back and nearly managed to corner him, but that was when he—it revealed its true fangs. It used an ability that only the Void Hunter should be capable of wielding, instantly killing and vaporizing one of our soldiers with nothing more than a touch!"
"At that point, we ran like our lives depended on it..."
Yuan was left speechless after hearing the soldiers' recollection of their encounter.
'These guys are lying off their asses!' he cried inwardly.
"Can you go into more detail about this Impersonator?" one of the representatives asked.
"When we encountered it, it had taken on the appearance of a soldier from Gaia's Heaven."
The Supreme General raised an eyebrow upon hearing this, while several others turned to look in his direction.
Of course, this alone meant nothing beyond the fact that the Impersonator had taken the appearance of someone from their city.
The soldiers described the Impersonator's appearance a moment later.
"It had black hair, brown eyes, a tall stature, and..."
As the Supreme General listened to the description of the Impersonator, a certain face surfaced in his mind. He felt an urge to turn around and look at Yuan, but managed to restrain himself.
'Surely, it must be a coincidence...' he tried to convince himself.

Once the soldiers finished speaking, one of the representatives said, "I hope you have actual evidence to support this discovery. You can't seriously expect us to believe all of this based solely on the testimony of a few soldiers from your own city."

"We have arrived," the servant announced as they reached the gate.
When it opened, a single path was revealed, lined with flowers on both sides and leading toward another gate at the entrance of the massive white building.
Although they couldn't see them from where they stood, eight other similar paths surrounded the building, each designated for a different city.
The servant continued leading Yuan and the others into the building.
Inside, they were greeted by a grand hallway adorned with paintings and other works of art.
Although they couldn't see them from where they stood, eight other similar paths surrounded the building, each designated for a different city.
The servant continued leading Yuan and the others into the building.
Inside, they were greeted by a grand hallway adorned with paintings and other works of art.
At the end of the hallway stood a large door that opened into a spacious white chamber with a massive circular table at its center.
Nine seats were arranged around the table, each marked with a distinct flag representing one of the nine cities.
Just as the representatives of Gaia's Heaven stepped into the room, the representatives from the other eight cities entered as well.
Without exchanging a word, the highest-ranking authority from each group made their way to the table and took their seats, while everyone else remained standing along the walls.
Once all of the seats were occupied, a tenth individual stepped forward and spoke loudly, "Gaia's Heaven."
"Present," the Supreme General said aloud.
"Spirit City."
"Present."
The man continued calling out every single city one by one.
"Ember City...
Eastern Dawn...
Mirage City...
Rising Sun...
Cloudpiercer...
Jade City...
Heavenly Furnace..."
"Present."
Once all nine cities had been called and accounted for, the man announced, "The assembly will now begin."
However, a long moment passed, and nobody spoke.
Instead, eight of the nine people at the table turned their attention to the representative from Ember City, the one who had called the assembly.
The representative from Ember City cleared his throat before speaking.
"I called for this assembly for one reason—to talk about a new enemy that may pose a serious threat to humanity.
I'm sure you've all heard the rumors by now, but we recently discovered a new type of Void Specter... one capable of perfectly disguising itself as a human."
No one responded or showed any surprise upon hearing this, as they had all already learned about it through the investigation not long ago.
"I will now allow the soldiers who encountered this Void Specter, which we have nicknamed the Impersonator, to recount their experience."
At his gesture, several soldiers stepped forward.
Yuan raised an eyebrow when he recognized them.
They were the same soldiers he had encountered in the Black Zone.
"My name is..."
The soldiers introduced themselves before recounting their encounter with Yuan.
"We were carrying out a mission in the Black Zone when we came across what appeared to be a lone, lost soldier.
At first, we thought he might need help, so we approached him."
"However, the moment we got close, he suddenly attacked us and killed one of our men.
We fought back and nearly managed to corner him, but that was when he—it revealed its true fangs.
It used an ability that only the Void Hunter should be capable of wielding, instantly killing and vaporizing one of our soldiers with nothing more than a touch!"
"At that point, we ran like our lives depended on it..."
Yuan was left speechless after hearing the soldiers' recollection of their encounter.
'These guys are lying off their asses!' he cried inwardly.
"Can you go into more detail about this Impersonator?" one of the representatives asked.
"When we encountered it, it had taken on the appearance of a soldier from Gaia's Heaven."
The Supreme General raised an eyebrow upon hearing this, while several others turned to look in his direction.
Of course, this alone meant nothing beyond the fact that the Impersonator had taken the appearance of someone from their city.
The soldiers described the Impersonator's appearance a moment later.
"It had black hair, brown eyes, a tall stature, and..."
As the Supreme General listened to the description of the Impersonator, a certain face surfaced in his mind.
He felt an urge to turn around and look at Yuan, but managed to restrain himself.
'Surely, it must be a coincidence...' he tried to convince himself.
Once the soldiers finished speaking, one of the representatives said, "I hope you have actual evidence to support this discovery.
You can't seriously expect us to believe all of this based solely on the testimony of a few soldiers from your own city."

chapters.title: Chapter 2679 The Impersonator
paragraphs: "Evidence? Of course, we have evidence," said Ember City's representative. "But before we get into that, I'd like to hear everyone's thoughts on the subject."
"Honestly, there's not much to think about, especially when we know so little about the Impersonator," said Spirit City's representative.

"I agree with that sentiment. So far, all we know is that it can kill someone with the slightest touch—something every Void Specter is already capable of. What makes this one so special aside from its ability to disguise itself as a human?" the representative from Cloudpiercer remarked.
The other representative expressed similar thoughts.
The Supreme General, who was the last to speak up, asked while looking at the soldiers who had the encounter, "When you ran away from the Impersonator, did it chase after you?"
"No... it did not."

The Supreme General narrowed his eyes and continued, "So you're telling me that even though it attacked you without provocation, it didn't even try to pursue you when you fled? That doesn't sound right at all."
"It's an abnormal existence, so we can't judge it by conventional logic," the representative from Ember City replied.
"So there's a chance this Impersonator isn't actually dangerous."
"How can you say that when it already killed two of our soldiers without provocation?" the representative from Ember City frowned.
"We don't know for certain whether it was truly unprovoked," the Supreme General replied. "And I'm not someone who accepts claims so easily without evidence."
"Enough yapping and show us your evidence already," said the Heavenly Furnace's representative. "This place is too cold, and I want to return home as soon as possible."
Nobody there but Yuan was puzzled by the man's remark about the place being too cold, as the room was only slightly cool from the air conditioning.
"Alright. Allow me to show you the evidence..."
The representative from Ember City made a gesture, and a screen suddenly appeared on the table before each representative.
Soon, a video began playing on the screen.
"I'm Captain Heen, and I'll brief you on this monster while we make our way to its location."
The video appeared to have been recorded from Captain Heen's perspective as he addressed a squad of soldiers.
"This is a recording of our investigation on the Impersonator," said Ember City's representative.
"A recording...?" Yuan muttered in a dumbfounded voice.
The footage flickered, and the next scene showed Captain Heen hovering above hundreds of Unknown Ores scattered across the ground, forming a clear trail.
"This is the place. Look at the ground. The Unknown Ores he left behind are still here!"
"It feels like a trap, as though someone deliberately left these ores behind to lure us in..."
"What should we do? It's clearly inviting—provoking us."
"There's only one thing we can do. Our mission."
"Stay alert, everyone. And don't engage without instructions."
The footage showed the soldiers following the trail of Unknown Ores for a few moments before flickering again.
The next scene showed Captain Heen and the soldiers encountering soldiers from another city, and they appeared to be gathering the Unknown Ores on the ground.
"Those are my soldiers!" the representative of Spirit City exclaimed after seeing these soldiers. "And they have been missing for some time now!"
"Just keep watching. It will explain what happened to them."
Yuan observed the situation in silence. He could already tell where things were headed, so he began considering how he should respond once it was his turn to get involved.
Meanwhile, the recording continued.
"Soldiers of Ember City?!"
"W-We're being ambushed!"
"Wait! We're not here for you, soldiers of Spirit City!"
"What?"

"We're currently investigating a certain entity, and we've been following the trail of Unknown Ores it left behind. However, the trail abruptly ended here, so we suspected that it might have entered this tunnel."
"Is that true?! A new type of Void Specter has been discovered?!"
"Of course it's true. Why would we lie about something like this? This Void Specter has already killed two of our soldiers."
"What does this Void Specter look like? Any special characteristics?"
"You'll probably find this hard to believe, but this Void Specter looks exactly like a human. Indistinguishable, too."

"Anyway, this Void Specter is currently disguised as a soldier from Gaia's Heaven. He has a tall, refined build, long black hair tied into a ponytail, brown eyes, and a strikingly handsome face. If you encounter him, do not engage under any circumstances. Run away immediately."
"Oh, right. He's also wearing the insignia of a corporal."
The reactions of Spirit City's soldiers were clearly captured on camera.
"That reaction... did you see this monster?"
"H-He went that way..."
The footage flickered again, conveniently skipping over the Spirit Soldier's mention of Yuan clearing the tunnel by himself.
"The first time we encountered him, he wasn't alone."
"Are you saying that there are actually two of these monsters wandering this land?!
"No...? That other individual with him is someone you should be familiar with, given her vast reputation."
"Who is this person?"
"It's the Ironwoman."
After seeing her name mentioned, the Supreme General and everyone in the room turned to look at the Ironwoman.
However, none of them spoke up, as they decided to wait until the end of the video and returned to watching it.
As for the Ironwoman, despite standing still and appearing calm on the surface, she was sweating profusely inside.
'It's over!' she cried inwardly.
The recording continued.
"Why are you all looking at me like I'm crazy?! Think about it! Would a mere corporal really be able to survive in the Black Zone for this long if he weren't actually a Void Specter in disguise?!"
"Do you mind if we come with you?"

"You can follow us if you want. However, keep some distance from us. With both groups together, we'd exceed ten people, and I'd rather not risk attracting the Void Hunter while we're already dealing with an unknown Void Specter."

The recording then showed them following the trail of Unknown Ores and eventually reaching their target. Of course, it skipped some of their conversation, including the Spirit City soldiers expressing doubt about the subject.
"I-It's him! It's definitely him!"
The footage zoomed in on the Impersonator's face and paused on it.
The moment the Supreme General and everyone from Gaia's Heaven recognized it, they immediately turned to look at Yuan.
Colonel Gu could hardly believe his eyes. He stood there frozen, staring at Yuan like a wooden statue, but that didn't last long.
"Y-You?!" Colonel Gu couldn't hold his voice for more than a moment and cried out loud, drawing the attention of everyone there.
"What's the commotion?" asked one of the representatives.
"H-Him! It's him!" Colonel Gu didn't hesitate and immediately exposed Yuan. "He's the Impersonator!"
"What?!"
Realizing that he could no longer remain silent, Yuan removed his mask, revealing his handsome face to everyone present.
"It's him! It's really him! The Impersonator!"
The soldiers from Ember City cried out in terror, as though they had suddenly been forced to relive a traumatic experience.
The very next moment, almost every single soldier in the chamber withdrew their weapon and pointed it at Yuan.
Seeing this, Yuan shook his head and sighed, "Boy, this sure escalated quickly."

chapters.title: Chapter 2680 The Impersonator(2)
paragraphs: "What the hell do you think you're all doing?!"
A thunderous voice suddenly erupted through the chamber.
The Supreme General rose from his seat and continued, "Have you all forgotten where we are right now?! Unless there is an active threat, it is prohibited to draw your weapons!"
"But there's an active threat standing right there! The Impersonator is in this very room!" the representative from Ember City exclaimed as he pointed at Yuan.
"Bullshit!" the Supreme General snapped back. "Nothing in that video proves he's the Impersonator—or that such a creature even exists!"

Then, the Heavenly Furnace representative gestured toward his soldiers and spoke, "Lower your weapons. Supreme General Tian is correct in this situation. Everything in the video so far is only hearsay. Just because they called him the Impersonator doesn't immediately make him one, nor have I seen any convincing evidence on the subject."
Once the soldiers from Heavenly Furnace lowered and put away their weapons, the others quickly followed suit. However, the soldiers from Ember City remained on high alert, their weapons still drawn.

"If you continue pointing your weapons at one of my soldiers, I will consider it a breach of the treaty—and a declaration of war against Gaia's Heaven," the Supreme General warned, his sharp gaze fixed on Ember City's soldiers.
"Put them away."
The Ember City representative turned toward them and gave the order.

A moment later, he continued, "Before we continue the recording, I would like to hear from that gentleman who resembles the Impersonator about what he was doing in the Black Zone alone. As far as I am aware, Corporals at Gaia's Heaven don't have the authority to leave the city alone, much less visit the Black Zone."
"At that time, I was lost," Yuan calmly responded.
"Lost? That doesn't explain why you're alone or why you're in the Black Zone."

"I won't go into the details since it mostly involves some drama with my fellow soldiers, but we were carrying out a mission in the Purple Zone. I ended up separating from them and entering the Black Zone, where I got lost because I had never been there before."
"Do you have anything to say about that, Supreme General Tian?"
"If you're asking whether I knew about his circumstances, then yes. I'm fully aware of why he was alone in the Black Zone, and he's not lying."
"Very well. Then let us continue watching the recording.
The footage continued the next moment, showing Yuan fighting the Void Specters and defeating them with ease.
"If he's also a Void Specter, why is he fighting other Void Specters?" someone commented after seeing this.
"Just keep watching," replied Ember City's representative.
"My lord! Do you see how fast he kills the Void Specters?! He's cleaning them up like trash!"
"I told you that guy isn't human!"
"How is he using so much energy when his cultivation is only at the Fifth Ascension? Where is he getting his power from?"
"Isn't it obvious?! He's recovering his energy from the Void Specters that he devours!"

"So he's the one digging up all those Unknown Ores and leaving them behind... No wonder he didn't seem the slightest bit interested in them before. But what could possibly be the purpose of doing that?"
"It's obviously a trap to lure us in! He knows how valuable Unknown Ores are to us, so he's using them as bait!"
The video flickered, skipping to the moment the atmosphere began changing.
"Th-This phenomenon! The Void Hunter... It's going to appear!"
"Shit! Shit! Shit! Do we run away?!"
"No! Not yet! Not until we see how that monster will respond to the Void Hunter!"
Almost everyone in the chamber drew a sharp breath the moment the Void Hunter appeared.

Even though they were only watching recorded footage, its unfathomable presence seemed to radiate through the screen, making it feel as though the Void Hunter were standing in the room with them at that very moment.
"They're really going to fight!"

The footage then showed the Void Hunter striking Yuan squarely in the stomach, an attack that should have ended his life instantly, as anything touched by the Void Hunter was supposed to be vaporized into thin air.
Yet, Yuan did not die and was merely sent flying into the distance.
"H-He survived?!" The Rising Sun's representative exclaimed in shock after witnessing someone survive the Void Hunter's physical blow for the first time.
The recording continued.
"D-Did he just survive a punch from the Void Hunter?!"
"This confirms it! There's no way he's human if he can survive being touched by a Void Specter!"
The footage ended there, and the representative from Ember City spoke.

"The Impersonator and the Void Hunter went on to fight each other for several weeks. If any of you have been wondering who the Void Hunter was fighting during that incident, now you have your answer."
He pointed directly at Yuan and continued, "Any normal human would've vaporized if they were touched by the Void Hunter, unless they are a Void Specter wearing human skin!"
The room fell silent as everyone turned their attention to Yuan, seemingly waiting for him to explain himself.
Yuan then spoke.

"So I'm a Void Specter just because the Void Hunter decided to spare me for some reason? Why did you stop the footage there? I'm sure you recorded my entire fight with the Void Hunter—or, more accurately, the Void Hunter beating my ass for weeks straight. Why aren't you showing that part?"

"Because all of that is irrelevant. The recording ended with the Void Hunter killing every one of my soldiers, along with the soldiers from Spirit City. Yet somehow, you're still alive. Why is that? Is it because you're the same kind of creature as the Void Hunter? And why aren't you affected by its touch?"

Yuan sighed. "Unfortunately, I can't explain why the Void Hunter chose to spare me while killing everyone else. For the record, I'm just as curious about the reason as you are. As for how I managed to survive its physical attacks... it was probably because of my physique, though I can't say for certain."
